control.description: true on the baseline arm every other arm is compared to

key.description: the arm's slug, unique within the experiment

payload.description: opaque JSON the arm carries, which the consumer interprets

weight.description: its share of the rollout; the arms sum to 100

from.description:
From is the RFC3339 start of the metric window. Empty means all time, treated as a
single reporting period (see monthsBetween).

question.description:
Question is the plain-language question about the org's books, e.g. "what is my
MRR?". Longer than 2000 characters is truncated, never refused.

to.description: To is the RFC3339 end of the metric window. Empty means up to now.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is unix seconds when the filter was saved, server-assigned.

event.description:
Event is the analytics event a member must have fired. EMPTY MEANS NO
FILTER: the audience is then every mailable customer in the org, and no
warehouse is consulted.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned audience id ("aud_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the audience's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is unix seconds of the last write, server-assigned, and the key
the audience list is ordered by (newest first). A saved audience has no
update route, so in practice it stays equal to CreatedAt: to change a
filter you save another one.

windowDays.description:
WindowDays is how far back the event counts, ending now. 0 means 30 and
nothing above 3650 is honoured. Ignored when Event is empty.

url.description: URL is the upstream server, http(s)://host[:port].

weight.description: Weight is this member's share of the round-robin; must be >= 0.

override.description:
Override books this bill even when one of the SAME economic identity
(vendor, total, issue date) already posted — the explicit human confirmation that a
same-looking bill is a genuine second spend, not the same receipt re-scanned.

scanId.description:
ScanID is the scanned document's file hash, as GET /v1/books/inbox and the scan
draft report it. It is the idempotency key: re-booking the same scan writes nothing.

voucher.description:
Voucher is the reviewed voucher to post. Its source is FORCED to (scan, scanId)
server-side, so it can never be booked under another source's key.

body.description: Body is the post text. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the target network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube or threads. Required — a post must name where it goes.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is unix seconds when the post was added, server-assigned and
never rewritten.

error.description:
Error is the exact reason the last publish attempt failed — the honest
record behind a "failed" status, never a faked success.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

publishedAt.description: PublishedAt is when the publish succeeded; 0 until it does.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix publish time; 0 leaves the post a draft, and any
value makes it "scheduled" for the durable sweep to pick up.

status.description: Status is draft, scheduled, published, failed or canceled. Server-owned.

title.description: Title is the post's internal label, capped at 1024 bytes.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is unix seconds of the last write, server-assigned. The durable
sweep writes too — claiming a due post, publishing it and recording a
failure each bump it — so this moves without anyone editing the post.

budget.description:
Budget is what the campaign is allowed to cost, in USD cents. A negative
value is clamped to 0; nothing enforces the ceiling here.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is unix seconds when the campaign was registered. Server-assigned
and never rewritten — an update leaves it as it was.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the campaign's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the free-text goal ("signups"), capped at 1024 bytes.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix send time; 0 means unscheduled. Setting it on a
campaign with no explicit status makes that status "scheduled".

spend.description:
Spend is what the campaign has cost so far, in USD cents, clamped to >= 0.
The CALLER owns it: no send, ad buy or invoice moves it, so it changes only
when create or update carries a new value. It is summed across the org's
campaigns into GET /v1/marketing/summary.

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, scheduled, active, paused or completed.
Empty means draft.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is unix seconds of the last write. Server-assigned on create and
on every update or schedule change, and the campaign list is ordered by it,
newest first.

id.description: ID is the cart to amend, from the path.

product.description:
Product names the catalog product to set, by its id or its URL slug. Give
this or Variant, never both; a request naming neither is refused.

quantity.description:
Quantity is how many of that item the cart should hold AFTER this call — it
is the resulting count, not a delta, so sending 3 twice leaves 3 and not 6.
ZERO REMOVES the line, which is the only way to take an item out.

variant.description:
Variant names the specific sellable variant to set, by its id or its SKU.
Prefer it over Product for anything sold in sizes, colours or tiers — the
price and the stock are the variant's, not the product's.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO 4217 code the cart is priced in, lower-cased. Empty
means usd.

email.description:
Email is the shopper's address, for a cart that belongs to someone who has
not signed in. It is what a guest checkout and an abandoned-cart follow-up
key on. Empty is fine.

store.description:
Store is the storefront this cart is being filled on. Empty uses the org's
default store, which is what a single-storefront merchant always wants.

user.description:
User is the id of the signed-in shopper this cart belongs to, when there is
one. Empty means a guest cart identified only by its own id.

account.description:
Account is the provider account this channel runs under: an ad-account, a page
or a mailing-list id. An executor may replace it at launch with the account it
actually used.

detail.description:
Detail is the last outcome in one secret-free line — the failure reason, or
what the executor reported. Absent when there is nothing to explain.

externalId.description:
ExternalID is the provider-side id of the running execution, recorded by the
orchestrator at launch and handed back verbatim to read spend or to pause.
Server-owned and absent until this channel has launched; anything a caller
sends for it is dropped.

kind.description:
Kind is the channel and the identity a campaign holds at most one of: paid,
organic or email. It picks the executor the launch fans out to.

platform.description:
Platform is the provider within the kind — meta, google, x, instagram, or the
email provider.

status.description:
Status is this channel's own launch outcome, not the campaign's: pending (added,
never launched), live, paused, failed (Detail says why) or unavailable (no
executor wired on this deployment). Server-owned — a caller can never assert it.

id.description:
ID is the file's path RELATIVE to its session's artifact directory, which is
also how it is fetched: GET /v1/exec/download/{session}/{id}.

name.description:
Name is the display name. On an ANSWER it carries the `{session}/{id}`
identifier whole, because the client matches on that prefix.

session_id.description:
SessionID is the other accepted spelling of the same fact on the way IN. Both
are read; whichever is set wins.

storage_session_id.description:
StorageSessionID names the session holding the bytes, and is the spelling the
answer always uses.

args.description:
Args become the PROGRAM's argv, never the compiler's. For the compiled
languages the toolchain builds first and these are passed to the binary it
produced.

code.description:
Code is the WHOLE program, not a fragment: it is written to a single file and
that file is what runs, so a compiled language needs its entry point and an
interpreted one runs top to bottom.

files.description:
Files are inputs the host already put in some session. Each names the session
its bytes live in, which is usually — and ideally — the session this run wants.

lang.description:
Lang selects the toolchain, and with it the filename the code is written to
and the line that runs it: py, js, ts, bash, r, php, go, rs, c, cpp, java, d,
f90. Anything else is refused rather than guessed at — a run in the wrong
language fails somewhere deep in a compiler, which reads as an outage.

runtime_session_hint.description:
RuntimeSessionHint is the stateful-session hint. It is carried so a client
that sends it is not silently misread, and it selects nothing here: every
session in this implementation is already a warm sandbox, so there is no
second kind of runtime for a hint to choose between.

session_id.description:
SessionID continues an EXISTING sandbox, which is what makes runs stateful:
the same filesystem, so one run's output file is the next run's input. Empty
leases a fresh sandbox and the id it got comes back on the result.

user_id.description:
UserID attributes the run inside the caller's org. It is a label, never a
tenant: the org is resolved from the validated principal and a value here
cannot widen what the run may reach.

max_age.description: MaxAge caps message age, e.g. "24h" or "7d"; "0" (default) is unlimited.

max_bytes.description: MaxBytes caps the stream's total stored bytes; -1 (default) is unlimited.

max_msg_size.description: MaxMsgSize caps one message's size in bytes; -1 (default) is the broker's limit.

max_msgs.description: MaxMsgs caps the number of stored messages; -1 (default) is unlimited.

name.description: Name is the stream name, unique within the org (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores).

num_replicas.description: Replicas is the number of stream replicas (1–5); this plane runs 1.

retention.description: Retention is the retention policy: limits (default), interest, or workqueue.

storage.description: Storage is the storage backend: file (default) or memory.

subjects.description: Subjects are the org-relative subjects bound to this stream (wildcards supported). Default: the stream name.

tech.description: who is reached about technical matters

params.description:
Params are the statement's bound values, in the order its `?` placeholders
appear — a string, a number, a boolean or null, whatever the column takes.
Absent means the statement carries no placeholders; bind values here rather
than interpolating them into the statement.

sql.description:
SQL is the statement to run. Blank (or absent) is refused before anything
reaches D1.

id.description: ID is the sandbox whose lease ends, from an earlier lease.

purge.description:
Purge deletes the project's DISK as well. It is opt-in because the disk holds
the only copy of the checkout: ending a lease is cheap and reversible,
deleting someone's uncommitted work is neither.

address.description:
Address is a single recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) before
use. Give this OR audienceId, never both and never neither.

audienceId.description:
AudienceID fans the sequence out over a saved audience, resolved live to
the org's mailable customers. Email only.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface; empty means email. An audience resolves
mailboxes, so an audience enroll must be email.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

key.description:
Key is the variable's name in the container, which must match
`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`. For a sealed value it is also the last segment
of the KMS ref, so it is what identifies the value across a round trip.

secret.description:
Secret says the value lives in KMS and never in the database. A caller may
only ADD secrecy: the server seals a value whose key or shape looks like a
credential anyway (secretshape.go), so an entry can come back secret that
was not sent that way.

value.description:
Value is the plaintext, and it is WRITE-ONLY once the entry is secret: a
sealed value reads back as "", and sending "" again KEEPS what is sealed
rather than wiping it. Only a non-empty value seals a new one.

key.description:
Key is the identifier the body substitutes ({{.key}}) and the key a
generation's data map must carry. snake_case by convention across the
built-ins — effective_date, company_name, governing_law. An override whose
body references a key no Field declares is refused on save.

label.description:
Label is the human prompt for whoever fills the value in — "Governing law
(state)". It never reaches the rendered document; only Key does.

keywords.description:
Keywords keeps only items whose TITLE contains one of these,
case-insensitively. They are also the GDELT queries the feed fans out to,
one per keyword of three characters or more — so a keyword both widens what
is fetched and narrows what is kept.

regions.description:
Regions keeps only items whose TITLE contains one of these, matched
case-insensitively as a substring. Empty keeps every region.

sources.description:
Sources keeps only items whose outlet name contains one of these,
case-insensitively. Empty keeps every outlet.

type.description: PIECE | CODE | ROUTER | LOOP_ON_ITEMS
PIECE_TRIGGER | EMPTY

decidedBy.description:
DecidedBy is who settled a terminal KYC status: the provider name, or a
reviewer's user id.

email.description:
Email is the founder's email, and the key a KYC decision addresses a founder
by — POST /v1/company/kyc/decision matches on it.

equityBps.description:
EquityBps is the founder's ownership in basis points, 0–10000 (1% == 100 bps,
so 10000 is the whole company). The founders' shares seed the cap-table genesis.

kycRef.description: KYCRef is the idv provider's session reference for this founder.

kycStatus.description:
KYCStatus is the founder's identity-verification state: pending, verified (a
real idv provider reported a pass), reviewer_confirmed (a privileged reviewer
confirmed out-of-band) or failed. The payment stage is unreachable until every
founder passes.

name.description: Name is the founder's full legal name, as it appears on the formation documents.

kind.description: asset kind: ecom|product|lifestyle|hover|hero

project.description: brand/site sub-scope (billing + tenancy axis)

tone.description: tone override for a single draft

voice.description: brand-voice guidance for the copy director

amount.description: Amount is the line total in whole cents (250000 is $2,500.00).

description.description: Description is the human-readable line, e.g. "Advisory retainer — August".

quantity.description: Quantity is the number of units, when the line is metered. Optional.

unitPrice.description: UnitPrice is the per-unit price in cents, when the line is metered. Optional.

class.description:
Class is what KIND of computer to lease, and the set is closed:

	exec     a throwaway one that keeps nothing. Seconds to minutes.
	dev      a coding one, with the project's own disk attached. Hours.
	desktop  a dev one that also has a screen.
	android  a desktop with a phone running on that screen.

Empty leases an `exec`, which is the right answer for running a program and
the wrong one for working on a repository, because it keeps nothing.

An `android` needs a node that can virtualise a CPU, so it is the one class
a deployment may not be able to place. Where the fleet has none, the lease
succeeds and the pod stays Pending naming the device it is waiting for —
which is the honest answer, because the alternative is an emulator running
on an interpreted CPU and never finishing its boot.

cluster.description:
Cluster names one of the org's ATTACHED clusters to run the lease on —
the fleet-local name a BYO cluster was registered under. Empty runs where
leases have always run, the home cluster. The named cluster must carry
the sandbox namespace and the gvisor runtime class; a name the org has
not attached is refused 404.

id.description:
ID names a sandbox to RESUME, and is the id an earlier lease answered with.
Empty asks for a new one. A caller that holds an id and omits it does not get
a second view of the same computer, it gets a second computer.

project.description:
Project names the disk to attach, and is REQUIRED for every class but `exec`.

One live sandbox per project: the disk attaches to one computer at a time, so
a second lease over a project that already has one is refused by name rather
than handed a silently empty disk.

runtime.description:
Runtime is the isolation boundary asked for: `gvisor` shares a filesystem
and holds a project volume, `kata-fc` is a microVM that boots slower and
reads files faster but has no shared filesystem at all. Empty asks for the
fleet's default, which is the right answer unless you are measuring.

It is a REQUEST. The owner decides, and refuses a combination it cannot
honour — a volume under a runtime with no shared filesystem would write
into a tmpfs and lose the bytes at exit. Read Leased.Runtime for what the
sandbox actually got.

ttlSec.description:
TTLSec bounds the lease in seconds. Unset takes the class default. Nothing
runs forever, because a sandbox is somebody else's code on our nodes.

account.description: Account is the chart-of-accounts number this side posts to, e.g. "5300".

credit.description: Credit is the leg's credit in exact cents. Set this or Debit, not both.

debit.description: Debit is the leg's debit in exact cents. Set this or Credit, not both.

load1.description:
Load1 is the machine's own one-minute load average — a count of runnable and
uninterruptible tasks, NOT a percentage and NOT already divided by core
count, so it is read against Spec.CPUs: 8.0 is idle on 16 cores and swamped
on 4. Coerced finite and non-negative on write, so 0 means either genuinely
idle or nothing reported.

load15.description:
Load15 is the same figure over fifteen. The three together are what separate
a machine that is busy right now from one that has been busy all along —
which is the question a dispatcher is really asking.

load5.description: Load5 is the same figure averaged over five minutes.

config.description:
Config is the transform's parameters: redirectScheme takes scheme (default
https) and permanent ("true" ⇒ 301, else 302); stripPrefix REQUIRES
prefixes (comma-separated, first match wins); addPrefix REQUIRES prefix;
headers is a header→value map set on the response.

id.description:
ID identifies the transform within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128
chars. A create that omits it gets a generated one. Routes reference it by
this id.

type.description: Type is the transform: redirectScheme, stripPrefix, addPrefix or headers.

build_command.description:
BuildCommand is what Cloudflare runs to build the site ("npm run build").
Omitted means no build step: the repository is published as it stands.

destination_dir.description:
DestinationDir is the directory the build leaves the site in ("dist"),
relative to RootDir. It is what gets served.

root_dir.description:
RootDir is where in the repository the build runs, for a project that is not at
the repository root. Omitted means the root.

id.description:
ID is the D1 database this binding points at, by Cloudflare's uuid. The binding
name the Worker code reads it as is the map key, not a field here.

compatibility_date.description:
CompatibilityDate pins which Workers runtime behaviour the functions run under,
as a date ("2024-01-01"). It is a pin, not a version: the runtime keeps that
date's semantics for code deployed against it.

compatibility_flags.description:
CompatibilityFlags turn individual runtime behaviours on or off ahead of, or
behind, the date above ("nodejs_compat").

d1_databases.description: D1Databases binds D1 databases in, keyed by binding name.

env_vars.description:
EnvVars are the environment variables the functions see, KEYED BY VARIABLE NAME.
The key is the name; the value carries the value and whether it is a secret.

kv_namespaces.description:
KVNamespaces binds KV namespaces into the functions, KEYED BY THE BINDING NAME
the code reads (`env.SESSIONS`). Same shape for the two below.

r2_buckets.description: R2Buckets binds R2 buckets in, keyed by binding name.

preview.description:
Preview is the config every branch build other than the production branch runs
under. It is a SEPARATE set of bindings and variables, which is what lets a
preview point at test data.

production.description: Production is the config the production branch builds under.

type.description:
Type is "plain_text" or "secret_text" and decides that: plain text is readable
afterwards, secret text is write-only. Empty is Cloudflare's default,
plain_text — so a secret with no type set is stored in the clear.

value.description:
Value is the variable's value. Under type "secret_text" Cloudflare encrypts it
on arrival and never reads it back, so a later read of the project shows the
variable without this.

namespace_id.description:
NamespaceID is the KV namespace this binding points at, by Cloudflare's id
rather than its title. The BINDING NAME — what the Worker code reads it as — is
the map key this value sits under, not a field here.

build_config.description: BuildConfig says how to build the site. Omitted means no build step.

deployment_configs.description:
DeploymentConfigs carries the preview and production runtime configs — the
bindings and variables the built site's functions run with.

name.description:
Name is the project name, and it is also the address: the site answers at
<name>.pages.dev. Cloudflare will not rename a project afterwards.

production_branch.description:
ProductionBranch is which git branch builds to production; every other branch
builds a preview. Omitted leaves Cloudflare's own default.

name.description:
Name is the R2 bucket this binding points at, by bucket name — R2 addresses
buckets by name where KV and D1 use ids. The binding name the Worker code reads
it as is the map key.

id.description: ID is the sandbox to read from, from an earlier lease.

path.description:
Path is read relative to the sandbox's working directory unless it is
absolute, and a path that climbs out of it is refused rather than rewritten.
Empty names the working directory itself, which lists it.

cache_paths.description:
CachePaths overrides CacheTTLSec per path PREFIX (key "/v1/models" → seconds).
The longest matching prefix wins.

cache_ttl_sec.description:
CacheTTLSec is the org's default edge-cache TTL for its responses, in seconds;
0 means no caching. Unset inherits the platform default.

cors_origins.description:
CORSOrigins is the PLATFORM-scope CORS allowlist EdgeCORS admits: an exact
origin, a bare host, or a "*.host" wildcard. Writable only by a SuperAdmin —
CORS is evaluated before identity, so it has no tenant to scope to.

methods.description:
Methods is the allowlist of HTTP methods the edge accepts for this org. Empty
means all are accepted.

mode.description:
Mode is the abuse gate's posture for THIS scope: "shadow" scores traffic and
records the verdict without acting on it, "live" enforces it. Unset means
shadow.

It is the one per-org field that does NOT inherit. Every other field here
layers a platform default under the org's own value, which is right for a
default: a tenant that sets no rate ceiling should get the platform's. Mode
is not a default, it is an ARMING DECISION — it is what makes a statistical
judgement start refusing real traffic — and inheriting it means arming one
scope arms every tenant that never asked for it, without a write to their
row and without anything in their config changing. So a tenant is live only
if that tenant's OWN row says live, and the platform row's mode governs
exactly one scope: the anonymous lane, which has no tenant of its own.

It is also not self-service. Writing it requires SuperAdmin (see the
/v1/gateway config op): the subject of an abuse control does not get to
switch the control off.

org_rpm.description:
OrgRPM is the org's OWN authenticated rate ceiling, requests per minute, as
ScopeRateLimit enforces it. Unset inherits the platform default, then the
static boot default.

per_ip_rpm.description:
PerIPRPM is the PLATFORM-scope pre-auth flood cap: requests EdgeRateLimit
admits per WindowSec from one client IP. SuperAdmin-only, same reason.

updated_at.description:
UpdatedAt is the unix second this policy row was last written. Server-stamped;
a client-supplied value is ignored.

updated_by.description:
UpdatedBy is the validated user id that wrote this policy row. Server-stamped;
a client-supplied value is ignored.

window_sec.description: WindowSec is the window PerIPRPM is counted over, in seconds. SuperAdmin-only.

arms.description: the blend — model ids from the arena

name.description: served as enso-<name>

doctype.description:
DocType is the content type holding the item: Campaign, SocialPost or Asset.
Any other name is refused as an unknown content type.

name.description:
Name is the document within that type — the item to distribute. Its caption,
media and channel list come off the stored document, so this names WHICH
item and says nothing about what goes out.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt hands a future go-live to the channel's own scheduler, as an
ISO-8601 time. Empty posts now.

filter.description: Filter purges only messages on this org-relative subject (wildcards supported).

keep.description: Keep retains that many newest messages.

name.description: Name is the stream name, from the path.

character.description:
Character is a 0-based UTF-16 code-unit offset within Line, per the LSP
specification — not a byte offset and not a rune index.

line.description: Line is 0-based, per the LSP specification.

path.description: Path is the repo-relative file, e.g. "apps/lsp/lsp.go".

relation.description:
Relation refines locate: definition, reference, type or implementation.
Empty means definition. Every other op ignores it.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository NAME within the caller's own org, e.g. "cloud".
Not a URL and not an owner/name pair: the owner is the validated
principal's org, so this names a repository the caller already owns.

rev.description:
Rev is a branch, tag or commit sha. Empty means the default branch. It is
resolved to a commit before anything else happens, so an answer is always
about one immutable tree.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO 4217 code, lower-cased. Empty means usd.

customerEmail.description: CustomerEmail is where the invoice is sent. Optional.

lines.description:
Lines are the charges. The invoice subtotal and amount due are COMPUTED
from these — there is no total field to send, because a total that
disagreed with its own lines would bill a number nobody could derive.

userId.description:
UserID identifies the customer being billed, within the caller's own org.
Required — an invoice with no addressee is not an invoice.

code.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

instrument.description:
Instrument identifies the payment method. It is the anti-farming key: one
redemption per instrument, fleet-wide, and it is REQUIRED — an absent
instrument is refused, never waved through.

key.description:
Key is the member: a domain, a CIDR or address, an issuer prefix, a
device digest. It is matched the same way the baseline is, so a deny on
tempbox.example also covers mail.tempbox.example.

note.description: Note is why, in your own words. Optional, bounded to 512 bytes.

verdict.description:
Verdict is allow or deny, and nothing else. An override is a decision —
unlike a baseline entry, which states facts and leaves the decision to your
policy — because your organisation is the only party entitled to say "for
us, this one is fine".

asOf.description:
AsOf is when the load happened, RFC 3339. Absent is dated on arrival, which
can only make the list look older than it is.

keys.description:
Keys is how many designations that load carried. Zero from a publisher who
designates somebody is a failed load wearing a successful one's clothes,
and belongs in Refusal instead.

refusal.description: Refusal is why the load failed, when it did.

source.description: Source is the publisher this receipt is for.

version.description:
Version is the digest of what that publisher supplied, so a refresh that
changed nothing can be told from a refresh that did not run.

force.description:
Force accepts a take whose size moved past the change bound. A publisher
serving a tenth or ten times its previous list is refused by default and the
previous version is left standing; this is the operator saying the change is
real. It cannot make an empty, truncated or unparseable take land — those are
errors, not magnitudes.

receipts.description:
Receipts are supplied by the component that holds the membership, for a set
of kind attest. They are refused on any other kind, and a set of kind attest
is refused without them: this plane never invents a freshness it did not
observe.

set.description: Set is the set to refresh.

companyName.description: the organisation the contact acts for

fax.description: fax number, in the same form as phone

doctypes.description: DocTypes restricts the semantic leg to a subset of indexed knowledge types.

index.description: Index names the lexical index to query. Defaults to "kb".

limit.description: Limit bounds the FUSED result set (default 10, max 50).

mode.description: Mode selects the legs: auto (default) | text | semantic | hybrid.

offset.description: Offset pages the fused result set.

project.description: Project narrows to one project scope within the org.

query.description: Query is the natural-language or keyword query. Required.

keys.description:
Keys are the values to look up, at most 100 per call: email addresses or
domains, IP addresses, card prefixes, user-agent strings, autonomous system
numbers, device digests.

sets.description:
Sets narrows which sets to consult. Empty consults every set whose matcher
can read the keys given.

country.description: Country is where they reside, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

name.description: Name is their full legal name as the IRS will hold it.

usTaxId.description:
USTaxID reports that they hold an SSN or ITIN. It is a BOOLEAN on purpose:
the number itself is never needed here and a field that could hold it is a
field that will eventually be logged.

glossary.description:
Glossary is the terminology the entry was translated under. Its VERSION — the
digest of the sorted terms — is part of the entry's identity, so editing a term
yields a new entry rather than overwriting the old rendering.

source.description:
Source is the ORIGINAL string this entry translates. Required; part of the
entry's identity, so a different source is a different entry.

state.description:
State is the entry's new position on the review ladder: suggested, approved or
published. `machine` is engine-only and is refused here — a human may not demote
a string back into the churn.

target.description:
Target is the target language tag (BCP-47, e.g. "es" or "pt-BR"). Required;
part of the entry's identity.

text.description:
Text is the reviewed translation to store. A human write always wins over the
stored value.

tier.description:
Tier is the engine tier the entry belongs to, quality (the default) or bulk.
Part of the entry's identity: the two tiers keep separate renderings.

name.description: Name is the round's name on the cap table, e.g. "Seed". Required.

preMoneyValuation.description: PreMoneyValuation is the valuation the round prices off, before the new money.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is the per-share price of a priced round.

roundType.description: RoundType is PRICED, SAFE or CONVERTIBLE_NOTE. Defaults to PRICED.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the cap table's share class the round issues into.

targetAmount.description:
TargetAmount is the amount the round is raising, recorded verbatim on the
canonical cap table's rounds.create contract.

host.description:
Host is the exact hostname this route matches, lowercased with any trailing
dot stripped. It is a GLOBALLY unique claim — one route across the whole
edge may hold a host, so no tenant can hijack another's.

id.description:
ID identifies the route within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128 chars.
A create that omits it gets a generated one.

middlewares.description:
Middlewares are the ids of the edge transforms to apply, in this order,
before the request reaches the service. At most 16.

pathPrefix.description:
PathPrefix narrows the match to requests under this path; it must start
with "/". Empty matches every path on the host.

priority.description:
Priority orders routes that share a host: higher wins, and equal priorities
fall back to the longer PathPrefix.

service.description:
Service is the id of the backend pool this route dispatches to. A route
naming a service that does not exist is skipped at compile, not served.

tls.description: TLS asks the edge to terminate TLS for Host with an ACME-managed certificate.

category.description:
Category is the COA expense account a matching bill books to. An upsert normalizes
a slug ("cloud") to its account number.

pattern.description:
Pattern is the merchant substring the rule matches on, case-insensitively. It is
also the key an upsert writes by.

priority.description: Priority breaks ties: when several patterns match, the highest wins.

argv.description:
Argv is the program and its arguments, already split — the form no shell can
misread. Give this or Command, not both.

blind.description:
Blind is the set of secrets this command must never publish.

It exists because output is redacted where it is PRODUCED or not at all. A
caller that scrubbed the returned result would still have streamed the
unredacted bytes into the session as they were written — to a durable event
store, an SSE feed and a chat thread — because the narration leaves the
sandbox by a different path from the result. Nothing downstream can take a
secret back out of a message that has already been delivered.

The sandbox holds these only for the life of the one command, applies them
to every stream leaving it, and never logs or stores them.

command.description:
Command is a shell line, run by `sh -c`. Use it when a pipeline or a
redirection is the point, and Argv when it is not.

dir.description:
Dir runs the command somewhere other than the sandbox's working directory,
which Leased.Workdir names.

id.description: ID is the sandbox to run in, from an earlier lease.

session.description:
Session is the live agent session this command narrates into: its output is
appended there AS IT IS PRODUCED, so every surface watching that session
watches the command work instead of a blank pause. A long run is otherwise a
silence with a verdict at the end.

It names a SESSION and never a tenant. The org is the one the caller already
proved, so a session belonging to somebody else is simply absent from the org
this call acts for and the append is refused there. Empty means nothing is
watching, and then nothing is sent.

stdin.description:
Stdin is fed to the program on standard input. This is how bytes reach a file
without being quoted into a shell line: `cat > path` with the contents here
writes them exactly.

timeoutSec.description:
TimeoutSec bounds this ONE command, so a wedged program holds the caller for
its own timeout rather than for the whole lease.

document.description:
Document is the raw CycloneDX bill of materials, any JSON. Its components[]
are flattened and persisted; nothing else is read or stored.

format.description: Format names the document format; "cyclonedx" is the only one parsed.

gitSha.description: GitSha is the commit the image was built from.

imageDigest.description:
ImageDigest is the content-addressed digest (sha256:…) the components are
keyed under. Required — it, not a tenant, is what an SBOM belongs to.

imageRef.description:
ImageRef is the human-readable image reference the digest was published as.
A resolve matches on either this or the digest.

sourceRepo.description: SourceRepo is the repository the image was built from.

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.

scheduledAt.description: ScheduledAt is the unix send time. 0 clears the schedule.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is unix seconds when the sequence was registered, server-assigned
and never rewritten.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned sequence id ("seq_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the sequence's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, active or archived. Empty means draft, and
ONLY an active sequence accepts enrollments.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is unix seconds of the last status flip, server-assigned, and the
key the sequence list is ordered by (newest first). Adding a step or
enrolling a contact does NOT touch it — only draft/active/archived does —
so it tracks activation rather than activity.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

status.description:
Status is draft, active or archived. Required; there is no default here,
unlike on create. Only an active sequence accepts enrollments.

entries.description: Entries are the overrides to write, up to 1000 per call.

email.description: Email is the address the signature request is sent to.

name.description: Name is the recipient's name, as it appears on the signature request.

gpus.description:
GPUs is every accelerator the machine advertises, one entry each, capped at
32 on write. Empty means the probe found none — and that is the answer a
Need is checked against, so a machine with no entry here clears no
accelerator floor. The list is not vendor-filtered: what satisfies a job is
counts and VRAM, never a brand (see Need).

body.description: Body is the message text. Required.

delaySeconds.description:
DelaySeconds is how long after the previous step this one sends (after
enrollment, for the first step). Must be >= 0.

id.description: SequenceID is the sequence id from the path (the route's :id).

subject.description: Subject is the email subject line, capped at 1024 bytes.

id.description:
ID is the sandbox to interrupt, from an earlier lease. Every command running
in it stops; the lease itself survives, so the checkout and the half-written
files are still there to read. Use EndIn to give the computer back.

atPeriodEnd.description:
AtPeriodEnd cancels at the end of the paid period rather than at once. It
defaults TRUE on the endpoint, because a customer who cancels has already
paid for the period they are in.

address.description:
Address is the recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) so an opt-out
cannot be slipped past on a case or whitespace difference. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the surface opted out of: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email. Opting out of one leaves the others reachable.

reason.description:
Reason is a free-text note, capped at 1024 bytes. The public one-click
endpoint records "one-click unsubscribe".

acmeEmail.description:
ACMEEmail is the ACME account email. It binds an account for the lifetime
of an edge process, so it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

extraHosts.description:
ExtraHosts get certificates without owning a route — at most 256. They feed
the ACME HostPolicy and hot-apply on the next reload.

staging.description:
Staging issues from Let's Encrypt's staging directory (untrusted certs, high
rate limits). Like ACMEEmail it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

backends.description: Backends are the upstream servers to balance across: 1..32 of them.

id.description:
ID identifies the pool within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128 chars.
A create that omits it gets a generated one. Routes reference it by this id.

passHostHeader.description:
PassHostHeader forwards the client's original Host header upstream instead
of rewriting it to the backend's.

framework.description: only when it differs from the template's

id.description: selector, unique within the template ("react", "grid-3-fluid")

kind.description: the axis it varies: format | page | theme

source.description: the repository this shape is forked from; the synthesized default shape carries the template's own

aliases.description:
Aliases are the other spellings a receipt may print the vendor under; a scan
matching any of them resolves to this vendor.

canonical.description: Canonical is the vendor's one true name, and the key an upsert writes by.

defaultCategory.description:
DefaultCategory is the COA expense account new bills from this vendor book to.
An upsert normalizes a slug ("software") to its account number.

description.description: Description is the human line for the event, e.g. the vendor a bill came from.

legs.description:
Legs are the sides of the posting. They must balance: Σdebit == Σcredit, give or
take the 2¢ round-off allowance.

postingAt.description:
PostingAt is the RFC3339 instant the event posts at — the time every statement
window filters on.

sourceId.description:
SourceID is the source event's own id within that namespace. Together with
SourceKind it is the key that makes a repeat posting a no-op.

sourceKind.description: SourceKind is the idempotency namespace naming what booked this, e.g. "scan".

bindings.description:
Bindings are the resources the script can reach (KV, D1, R2, secrets, …), in
Cloudflare's own binding vocabulary, passed through as written: this plane
deliberately does not model Cloudflare's shapes. Absent uploads a script with
NO bindings, which replaces whatever the previous version had.

compatibilityDate.description:
CompatibilityDate pins which Workers runtime behaviour the script runs under,
as a plain calendar date ("2024-01-01"). Absent leaves the account's own
default in force.

compatibilityFlags.description:
CompatibilityFlags turn individual runtime behaviours on or off around that
date ("nodejs_compat"), in Cloudflare's own flag vocabulary. Absent means the
date alone decides.

mainModule.description: MainModule is the module file the runtime starts at. Absent means "worker.js".

script.description:
Script means two things on this route, and the document says so in both places
it appears: the PATH segment names the Worker to publish, and the BODY field
carries that Worker's ES-module source — the code itself, never a name or a
URL. A blank or absent source is refused; there is no empty Worker.

data.description: Data is the file's bytes, and replaces whatever was there.

id.description: ID is the sandbox to write into, from an earlier lease.

path.description:
Path is confined the same way PathIn.Path is. Missing parent directories are
created.

id.description: ID is the accreditation record to decide, from the path.

status.description:
Status is the decision being recorded: reviewer_confirmed, provider_verified,
rejected, or expired.

basis.description:
Basis is the qualification category: income, net_worth, professional_license,
or entity.

evidenceDocId.description: EvidenceDocID references an evidence document in the org's sealed data room.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is the unix second a confirmation ages out; 0 means none.

method.description:
Method is how the state was established: self_attested, third_party_letter,
or provider_verified.

note.description: Note is a non-PII operator note.

status.description:
Status may only be "asserted" (empty reads as asserted); every confirmed,
rejected or expired state is recorded via the decision endpoint.

subjectId.description: SubjectID names the subject this record is about; it must exist within the org.

activate.description: Activate switches these tool names on for the caller's org and project.

deactivate.description: Deactivate switches these tool names off.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

host.description: Host is the hostname to attach. Required, and must be a valid DNS hostname.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

to.description:
To is the target stage: structure, founders, payment, documents, esign,
genesis, import or company.

accessGroups.description:
AccessGroups REPLACES the org's named access groups, as
group name -> channel -> entries. Absent or null leaves them alone.

channel.description:
Channel is the transport to edit: discord, github, linear, slack, teams, telegram or whatsapp.
Required; an unknown value is a 404.

dm.description:
DM REPLACES the config-managed DM allow entries. Absent or null leaves them
alone; an empty list clears them. It never touches senders approved through
pairing — a policy edit cannot revoke an approved pairing.

dmPolicy.description:
DMPolicy sets how direct messages are admitted: "pairing" (a person must be
approved first), "allowlist" (only listed senders) or "open". Empty leaves
it unchanged.

group.description:
Group REPLACES the config-managed group allow entries. Absent or null
leaves them alone; an empty list clears them.

groupPolicy.description:
GroupPolicy sets how group and thread rooms are admitted: "open",
"allowlist" or "disabled". Empty leaves it unchanged.

alpha.description:
Alpha overrides the 0.05 two-tailed significance threshold when it lies
strictly between 0 and 1; anything else leaves the default in place.

days.description:
Days is how far back to read when no start is given: 1 to 365, 30 by
default. A value outside that range leaves the default in place.

end.description: End is the window's exclusive end in RFC3339, defaulting to now.

id.description: ID is the experiment the URL names.

start.description: Start is the window's inclusive start in RFC3339. Given, it wins over days.

accent.description:
Accent is the one hue — a CSS colour token (a hex, or a bounded functional
colour like rgb()/oklch()). Anything else is dropped rather than stored.

density.description: Density is the spacing step: "compact", "default" or "comfortable".

type.description:
Type is the text-size multiplier, clamped to the ramp window [0.85, 1.4].
Absent (0) leaves the published default.

requestedCode.description:
RequestedCode is the vanity code the applicant asks for; approval may mint
a different one if it is taken. Body-only: the URL cannot supply it.

channel.description:
Channel is the transport the request came in on: discord, slack, teams,
telegram or whatsapp.

code.description:
Code is the pairing code from GET /v1/channels/pairing. It is a capability:
holding it is what authorises the approval, alongside org admin.

query.description: Query is the question, from the BODY. Takes precedence over `?q=`.

repo.description: Repo is the repository narrowing, from the BODY. Takes precedence over `?repo=`.

code.description:
Code is the affiliate code the referred org arrived with. Body-only: the
URL cannot supply it.

alreadyIncorporated.description:
AlreadyIncorporated declares an org that already has an entity, which takes
the import path (POST /v1/company/skip) instead of the formation path.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity to form: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

image.description:
Image is the toolchain image the recipe runs in, a Go bookworm image by
default. It is the one field the GitHub lane ignores: there the runner IS
the toolchain, and a cluster has to be told what a runner already is.

ldflags.description:
Ldflags are the Go linker flags, `-s -w` when the recipe names none, on one
line. Go lane only.

main.description:
Main is the Go package to build, repo-relative (`.` or `./cmd/x`), and it
selects the GO LANE. Defaults to `.` when neither lane is named; declaring
it together with `run` is refused.

name.description:
Name is the artifact's base name: the prefix of every file published for
this entry, and the name a host later asks for. It must match
`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, which is what makes it safe as both a
filename and a URL path segment.

out.description:
Out is the glob of files `run` produced, relative to the repo root; matching
nothing FAILS the build rather than publishing an empty entry. It expands
unquoted, so it is bounded to path and glob characters. The Go lane names
its own files and ignores this.

platforms.description:
Platforms are the `<os>/<arch>` pairs the Go lane cross-compiles, [linux/amd64]
by default. Each one publishes as `<name>-<os>-<arch>`, which is the shape a
host resolves a binary BY — so the list is what a caller can ask for later.

run.description:
Run is any other toolchain's build command, run by `sh -c` in this entry's
image, and it selects the OTHER LANE. Arbitrary shell is the point — it is
the same trust as a Dockerfile RUN — which is why it executes with no
object-store credential and no service-account token. It requires `out`.

agentName.description: AgentName is the cloud Agent (/v1/agents) the machine will run. Required.

botVersion.description: BotVersion pins the @hanzo/bot runtime version; empty takes the default.

id.description: ID is the machine to bind, from the URL path.

name.description: Name is the bucket name to create.

Name is the bucket's friendly name, matching
^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$. It is validated AS GIVEN and never
lower-cased for you: a client that creates "Photos" and then lists "photos"
would be reading a bucket it did not make, so mixed case is a clean 400.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps, 1–64. 0 means 1.

maxValue.description:
MaxValue caps one value's size in bytes. 0 or less means the server's
ceiling.

ttl.description: TTL expires entries after this many SECONDS. 0 means no expiry.

name.description:
Name is the plugin's name: one lowercase path segment (a-z0-9, _ or -),
and the id the runtime loads it by.

provider.description:
Provider is the connectors provider whose credential the plugin reads at
run time. Empty for a plugin that needs none.

source.description: Source is TypeScript to build as-is. Exactly one of Source or Spec.

spec.description:
Spec is API documentation — an OpenAPI document, or prose describing the
endpoints — that the generator turns into Source. The generated source is
returned in the response, so a caller can read what will run before it runs.

data.description:
Data is the payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).
Binary payloads belong on the NATS port.

headers.description:
Headers are optional message headers, one value per name. A Nats-Msg-Id
header is JetStream's deduplication key: a repeat within the stream's
dedup window is acknowledged as duplicate rather than stored twice.

subject.description:
Subject is the subject to publish to, in the org's own namespace — e.g.
orders.created. No wildcards.

data.description: Data is the request payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are optional request headers, one value per name.

subject.description: Subject is the subject a responder listens on, in the org's namespace.

timeoutMs.description:
TimeoutMs bounds the wait for a reply. 0 or less means the default of
5000; anything above 30000 is clamped to 30000.

e164.description:
E164 is the number to buy, in E.164 (a leading + and digits), exactly as the
search returned it. This is the number itself, not the id from a search result.

agent.description:
Agent hands the answered call to a Hanzo assistant by name instead of
connecting it to a person. Empty places an ordinary call.

from.description: From is the number to call FROM, in E.164. It must be one this org holds.

record.description:
Record is a per-call flag rather than a product. Where a recording lands and
how long it is kept is the org's retention policy, not this call's.

to.description: To is the number to call, in E.164.

webhook.description:
Webhook is a URL the carrier posts this call's events to as it progresses.
Empty means the call's outcome is only visible by reading it back.

account.description: Account is the provider ad-account this campaign runs on (Meta act_<id>). Optional.

budget.description: Budget is the campaign budget in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

name.description: Name is the campaign's display label. Required; trimmed and bounded to 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the campaign goal as the provider names it. Optional, bounded to 1024 bytes.

platform.description: Platform is the ad network: meta, google, tiktok or x. Empty defaults to meta.

spend.description: Spend is the amount spent so far in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

status.description: Status is the lifecycle state: draft, active, paused or completed. Empty defaults to draft.

id.description: ID is the campaign to update, from the path.

audience.description: Audience is the segment or audience selector this campaign targets.

budget.description: Budget is the campaign's total budget in CENTS. Negative reads as 0.

channels.description:
Channels are the fan-out targets, at most one per kind (paid, organic,
email) and at most 12. A channel's status and provider id are server-owned:
whatever the caller sends for them is replaced with "pending".

content.description:
Content is the ordered creative set. Content[0] is the active creative and
the rest are A/B variants; at most 32, empty entries dropped.

name.description:
Name is the campaign's display name. Required; trimmed and capped at 2048
characters.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when the campaign should run, in unix seconds. Negative reads
as 0 (immediately).

incorporationCountry.description:
IncorporationCountry is the ISO country the entity is incorporated in.
Optional; omitted, null or empty clears it. Any JSON scalar is accepted
and stored as its text.

name.description:
Name is the company's legal name. Required, and it must be a non-empty
string — anything else is refused with the cap table's own validation
error.

additionalTerms.description: AdditionalTerms is free text for anything the fields above do not carry. Optional.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved it, YYYY-MM-DD.

capital.description: Capital is the principal lent, in the company's currency.

conversionCap.description: ConversionCap is the valuation the note converts at, at most. Optional.

discountRate.description: DiscountRate is the discount to the next round's price, as a percentage. Optional.

interestRate.description: InterestRate is the annual interest the principal accrues, as a percentage. Optional.

issueDate.description: IssueDate is when the note was issued, YYYY-MM-DD.

publicId.description: PublicID is the note's identifier. It must be UNIQUE within the company; reusing one is refused 409.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID is the lender. It must name a stakeholder of THIS company.

status.description: Status is DRAFT, ACTIVE, PENDING, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.

type.description: Type is CCD, OCD or NOTE.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board adopted the plan, YYYY-MM-DD.

comments.description: Comments is a free-text note kept with the plan. Optional.

defaultCancellatonBehavior.description:
DefaultCancellatonBehavior is what happens to cancelled grants: RETIRE, RETURN_TO_POOL, HOLD_AS_CAPITAL_STOCK or DEFINED_PER_PLAN_SECURITY.

The key is spelled `defaultCancellatonBehavior` — one `l` — because that is
the wire, and correcting it here would silently drop the field.

initialSharesReserved.description: InitialSharesReserved is how many shares the plan may grant. A whole number.

name.description: Name is the plan's name, e.g. "2026 Stock Option Plan".

planEffectiveDate.description: PlanEffectiveDate is when the plan takes effect, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the class the plan grants from. It must name a class of THIS company.

amount.description:
Amount is the money invested, in the round's own currency. Required and must
be positive.

comments.description: Comments is a free-text note kept with the investment. Optional.

date.description:
Date is when the investment was made, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional: omitted, it is
recorded as today.

id.description:
ID is the round to invest in. The URL is the addressing authority — a path
segment binds after the body and after the query — so the address decides
which round is written whatever a body claims.

stakeholderId.description:
StakeholderID is the investor. Required, and it must reference a stakeholder
of the same company.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved the grant, YYYY-MM-DD.

cliffYears.description: CliffYears is how long before ANY of the grant vests. A whole number; 0 for no cliff.

equityPlanId.description: EquityPlanID is the plan the options come from. It must name a plan of THIS company.

exercisePrice.description: ExercisePrice is the strike price per share, in the company's currency.

expirationDate.description: ExpirationDate is when unexercised options lapse, YYYY-MM-DD.

grantId.description: GrantID is the grant's identifier. It must be UNIQUE within the company; reusing one is refused 409.

issueDate.description: IssueDate is when the grant was made, YYYY-MM-DD.

notes.description: Notes is a free-text note kept with the grant. Optional.

quantity.description: Quantity is how many options to grant. A whole number above 0.

rule144Date.description: Rule144Date is when the Rule 144 holding period starts, YYYY-MM-DD.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID is who receives the grant. It must name a stakeholder of THIS company.

status.description: Status is DRAFT, ACTIVE, EXERCISED, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.

type.description: Type is ISO, NSO or RSU.

vestingStartDate.description: VestingStartDate is when vesting begins, YYYY-MM-DD.

vestingYears.description: VestingYears is the total vesting period. A whole number.

closeDate.description:
CloseDate is the date to record the round as closed on. Optional: omitted,
null or empty records TODAY. Any JSON scalar is accepted and stored as its
text, and the text is stored unparsed, so a caller that wants an ISO date
sends one.

id.description:
ID is the round to close. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

name.description: Name is the round's name, e.g. "Series A".

preMoneyValuation.description: PreMoneyValuation is the company's valuation before the new money. Optional.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is the price investors pay per share. An investment into a round with a price ISSUES the shares it buys; one into a round priced later records the money alone.

roundType.description: RoundType is PRICED, SAFE or CONVERTIBLE.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the class investors receive. It must name a class of THIS company.

targetAmount.description: TargetAmount is how much the round aims to raise, in the company's currency.

additionalTerms.description: AdditionalTerms is free text for anything the fields above do not carry. Optional.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved it, YYYY-MM-DD.

capital.description: Capital is the money invested, in the company's currency.

discountRate.description: DiscountRate is the discount to the next round's price, as a percentage. Optional.

issueDate.description: IssueDate is when the SAFE was signed, YYYY-MM-DD.

publicId.description: PublicID is the SAFE's identifier. It must be UNIQUE within the company; reusing one is refused 409.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID is the investor. It must name a stakeholder of THIS company.

status.description: Status is DRAFT, ACTIVE, PENDING, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.

type.description: Type is PRE_MONEY or POST_MONEY — which side of the new money the cap is measured on.

valuationCap.description: ValuationCap is the valuation the SAFE converts at, at most. Optional; omit for an uncapped SAFE.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved the class, YYYY-MM-DD.

conversionRights.description: ConversionRights is CONVERTS_TO_FUTURE_ROUND or CONVERTS_TO_SHARE_CLASS_ID. The second requires convertsToShareClassId.

convertsToShareClassId.description: ConvertsToShareClassID names the class this one converts into. Required when conversionRights is CONVERTS_TO_SHARE_CLASS_ID, ignored otherwise.

id.description:
ID addresses the resource. The URL is the addressing authority — a path
segment binds after the body and after the query — so the address decides
which row is written whatever a body claims.

initialSharesAuthorized.description: InitialSharesAuthorized is how many shares this class may issue. A whole number.

liquidationPreferenceMultiple.description: LiquidationPreferenceMultiple is the multiple of invested capital paid out before junior classes — 1 for a 1x preference.

name.description: Name is the share class's name, e.g. "Series A Preferred".

parValue.description: ParValue is the nominal per-share value on the certificate, in the company's currency.

participationCapMultiple.description: ParticipationCapMultiple caps participation after the preference is paid, as a multiple of invested capital. 0 for no cap.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is the issue price for this class, in the company's currency.

seniority.description: Seniority orders liquidation preference: LOWER is more senior, so 1 is paid before 2.

stockholderApprovalDate.description: StockholderApprovalDate is when the stockholders approved it, YYYY-MM-DD.

votesPerShare.description: VotesPerShare is how many votes one share of this class carries. A whole number; 0 for non-voting.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved the class, YYYY-MM-DD.

conversionRights.description: ConversionRights is CONVERTS_TO_FUTURE_ROUND or CONVERTS_TO_SHARE_CLASS_ID. The second requires convertsToShareClassId.

convertsToShareClassId.description: ConvertsToShareClassID names the class this one converts into. Required when conversionRights is CONVERTS_TO_SHARE_CLASS_ID, ignored otherwise.

initialSharesAuthorized.description: InitialSharesAuthorized is how many shares this class may issue. A whole number.

liquidationPreferenceMultiple.description: LiquidationPreferenceMultiple is the multiple of invested capital paid out before junior classes — 1 for a 1x preference.

name.description: Name is the share class's name, e.g. "Series A Preferred".

parValue.description: ParValue is the nominal per-share value on the certificate, in the company's currency.

participationCapMultiple.description: ParticipationCapMultiple caps participation after the preference is paid, as a multiple of invested capital. 0 for no cap.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is the issue price for this class, in the company's currency.

seniority.description: Seniority orders liquidation preference: LOWER is more senior, so 1 is paid before 2.

stockholderApprovalDate.description: StockholderApprovalDate is when the stockholders approved it, YYYY-MM-DD.

votesPerShare.description: VotesPerShare is how many votes one share of this class carries. A whole number; 0 for non-voting.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved the issuance, YYYY-MM-DD.

capitalContribution.description: CapitalContribution is cash paid for the shares. Optional.

certificateId.description: CertificateID is the certificate number. It must be UNIQUE within the company; reusing one is refused 409.

cliffYears.description: CliffYears is how long before ANY of the grant vests. A whole number; 0 for no cliff.

companyLegends.description:
CompanyLegends are the restrictive legends printed on the certificate.

A LIST, and it must be sent as one: the bundle substitutes an EMPTY list for
anything that is not an array, so a single string would be accepted and
silently discarded — the certificate issued with no legends and nothing
reporting it.

debtCancelled.description: DebtCancelled is debt forgiven as consideration. Optional.

ipContribution.description: IPContribution is intellectual property assigned as consideration, valued in the company's currency. Optional.

issueDate.description: IssueDate is when the shares were issued, YYYY-MM-DD.

otherContributions.description: OtherContributions is any other consideration, valued in the company's currency. Optional.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is what was paid per share. Optional.

quantity.description: Quantity is how many shares to issue. A whole number above 0.

rule144Date.description: Rule144Date is when the Rule 144 holding period starts, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the class being issued. It must name a class of THIS company.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID is who receives the shares. It must name a stakeholder of THIS company.

status.description: Status is ACTIVE, DRAFT, SIGNED or PENDING.

vestingStartDate.description: VestingStartDate is when vesting begins, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; defaults to the issue date.

vestingYears.description: VestingYears is the total vesting period. A whole number; 0 for fully vested at issue.

certificateId.description:
CertificateID names the NEW certificate a partial transfer issues, and is
required for one — a partial transfer without it is refused 400. It is unused
by a full transfer, which reassigns the existing certificate.

It must be unique within the company; reusing one is refused 409. Declaring
it is not optional in the way the tag suggests: omitting this field from the
Go type would leave `quantity` accepted and every PARTIAL transfer answering
"certificateId is required" with no way for a caller to supply it — the
silent-drop failure this whole conversion was blocked on, one field wide.

quantity.description:
Quantity is how many shares to move. OPTIONAL, and its absence is not zero:
omitted or null transfers the WHOLE certificate. A value outside 1..held is
refused, so a partial transfer can never over-issue.

A full transfer REASSIGNS the certificate and mints no new one; a partial
transfer splits it and answers with the new share's id. That is the fact a
caller needs from the answer, not from this comment.

shareId.description:
ShareID is the certificate being transferred. Required, and it must name a
share in the caller org's own company — a share id from another tenant
resolves to not-found rather than to another company's certificate.

toStakeholderId.description:
ToStakeholderID is who receives them. Required, and it must reference a
stakeholder of the SAME company; one that does not is refused 400 rather
than creating a dangling holder.

currentRelationship.description:
CurrentRelationship is how the stakeholder relates to the company, e.g.
FOUNDER, INVESTOR or EMPLOYEE. This route stores it as sent — unlike
adding a stakeholder, it is not checked against the vocabulary.

email.description:
Email is the stakeholder's email. This route stores it as sent — unlike
adding a stakeholder, it is not checked for shape or uniqueness.

id.description:
ID is the stakeholder to update. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

institutionName.description: InstitutionName names the institution, when the stakeholder is one.

name.description: Name is the stakeholder's full name.

stakeholderType.description:
StakeholderType is INDIVIDUAL or INSTITUTION. This route stores it as
sent — unlike adding a stakeholder, it is not checked against the
vocabulary.

state.description: State is the stakeholder's state or province.

streetAddress.description: StreetAddress is the stakeholder's street address.

taxId.description: TaxID is the stakeholder's tax identifier.

zipcode.description: Zipcode is the stakeholder's postal code.

brands.description: Brands are the brands whose console shows it. Omit for every brand.

id.description: ID is the category slug to write, from the path.

label.description: Label is the display name. Required.

order.description: Order is where the category sits among its siblings, ascending.

summary.description: Summary is the one line describing what the category groups.

account.description:
Account is the provider account this channel runs under: an ad-account, a
page, or a mailing-list id.

id.description: ID is the campaign to add the channel to, from the path.

kind.description:
Kind is the channel kind and the identity a campaign holds at most one of:
paid, organic or email.

platform.description:
Platform is the provider within the kind — meta, google, x, instagram, or
the email provider.

channel.description: Channel is the transport to edit. Required; an unknown value is a 404.

default.description:
Default sets the agent for rooms with no binding of their own; "hanzo"
restores the built-in. Empty or absent leaves it unchanged.

rooms.description: Rooms binds platform room ids to agents; rooms not named are left alone.

unbind.description: Unbind removes the bindings of these rooms, so they fall back to Default.

message.description:
Message is the founder's question for the Business AI. Required; trimmed,
and clipped to 4 KiB so a caller cannot amplify the AI prompt.

code.description:
Code is the referrer's referral code, as it appeared in their ?ref= link.
Case and surrounding whitespace do not matter.

Code is the share-link code that was clicked. Body-only: the URL cannot
supply it.

default.description: Default marks this the org's default cluster for scheduling.

kubeconfig.description:
Kubeconfig is the cluster's kubeconfig, verbatim. Required — a body without
one is not an attach.

name.description:
Name is the fleet-local name for the cluster; lower-cased, and the key the
detach route addresses it by. Required.

provider.description:
Provider is a free-form label for where the cluster runs ("gke", "on-prem");
it is display only, not a routing key.

content.description: Content maps a document field to its ProseMirror markup JSON.

source.description:
Source is the blob ref a getContent reads the snapshot from. Absent means
there is no snapshot to read, which answers empty content.

updates.description:
Updates carries, per field, a base64 Y.js state update encoding the SAME
markup — the front computes it (markupToYDoc → encodeStateAsUpdate) so a
createContent seeds the live-editing lane's update log, not just the
snapshot blob. Without it a dialog-created description is invisible in the
collaborative editor, which replays the ydoc log, never the snapshot.

documentId.description:
DocumentID addresses the document field, as
"<spaceUuid>|<objectClass>|<objectId>|<objectAttr>" — the
collaborator-client encodeDocumentId shape, from the path.

method.description: Method is the verb: createContent, updateContent or getContent.

accountId.description:
AccountID is the provider account the credential should be scoped to, for the
providers whose Verify needs one (Cloudflare). Ignored by the OAuth path.

provider.description: Provider is the connector's registry id, from the :provider path segment.

token.description:
Token is the customer's provider credential. Its PRESENCE — not its value —
is what selects the apikey seal over the OAuth flow for a provider that
offers both: {"token":"…"}, even empty, is an apikey attempt (→ verify, which
answers the "token required" 400 on an empty value), while a body with no
token key (the console Connect button, `hanzo connector add` with no --token)
starts OAuth. Read on STDIN by the CLI, never argv; never logged or echoed.

githubLogin.description:
GithubLogin is the account to link. Used only when IAM holds no linked
account for the provider — a linked account is stronger proof and always wins.

login.description:
Login is the provider-neutral alias for GithubLogin, preferred when both are
sent.

provider.description: Provider is the forge to enrol with: github (the default) or gitlab.

budgetTokens.description:
BudgetTokens caps the bundle's size. Clamped to [256, 32000]; 0 or absent
uses 4000.

query.description: Query is what to retrieve context for. Required, max 4000 bytes.

repo.description:
Repo narrows retrieval to one repository. Empty searches every repo the org
has indexed.

id.description: ID is the session to steer, from the path.

message.description:
Message is free text for the running agent, up to 16 KiB. On a stop it is
recorded as the cancellation reason.

payload.description:
Payload is a structured argument for the command: any valid JSON up to
64 KiB, scanned for credentials before it is stored (a hit refuses the
command with 422 and the findings). A task-backed session receives it as
the forwarded signal's argument.

url.description:
URL is the page to read, absolute and http or https — no other scheme is
dialled. It is resolved from inside the cluster, so an address that turns out
to be loopback, link-local, private or multicast is refused at the dialer,
redirects included. Empty is not an error status: the answer comes back with
success false and the reason in error.

name.description:
Name is the account's label. Required, trimmed; it groups wallets and is
not itself a key.

avatar.description:
Avatar and Emoji are how the agent APPEARS. An image wins when both are
given — it is the thing somebody made — and both empty leaves the agent
drawn as its initial. Validated by iam/pkg/schema, the same rule a person's
avatar passes, so the 96 KiB bound and the accepted URL forms are stated
once for every subject that has a face.

computeRef.description:
ComputeRef optionally binds this bot to a visor machine. Opaque here, bounded
at 256 characters, and not resolved — this package stores the reference and
the binding's lifecycle belongs elsewhere.

description.description:
Description is the one line published as the description of the `agent_<name>`
tool, which is how another agent decides whether to call this one. Optional,
and worth writing for exactly that reason.

emoji.description:
Emoji is the single glyph shown when there is no image. An image WINS when
both are given — it is the thing somebody made — and both empty leaves the
agent drawn as its initial.

executionMode.description:
ExecutionMode is one-shot or long-running. Empty takes one-shot, which runs
only when something POSTs to it. long-running additionally requires Schedule,
and counts against a per-org cap that answers 409 when it is full.

instructions.description:
Instructions is the system prompt, up to 32 KiB, stored verbatim. This is what
the model reads; Description is what other CALLERS read.

model.description:
Model names the model to run on. Omit it to take the deployment's configured
default; name one and it is checked against the gateway's served catalogue
here, so a model this deployment cannot serve is refused now rather than at
the first run. Stored under our own name for it, whatever spelling arrives.

name.description:
Name is the agent's org-unique handle and the only required field. It must
match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, and a name already taken in this org
is a 409 rather than an overwrite. It is permanent: no update route moves it.

schedule.description:
Schedule is the 5-field cron a long-running agent fires on, parsed here so a
bad expression is a 400 and not an agent that silently never runs. Required
with long-running; DISCARDED for one-shot rather than stored unused.

serviceAccountId.description:
ServiceAccountID optionally names the IAM agent service account (<org>-<agent>)
a scheduled run should be billed AS, so an autonomous run is attributable to a
principal rather than only to the org. Same 256-character bound, also
unresolved here.

tools.description:
Tools are the tool names this agent may call. Omitted or empty grants NONE —
that default is the agent's authority and is not widened anywhere. The single
entry "*" means whatever the fleet's MCP server serves at the time of each run.

buildType.description:
BuildType is `pack` — the zero-config default that detects any project —
or `dockerfile`, the explicit escape hatch. An image app never builds.

description.description: Description is free text about what the application is.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile is the path to build from, for buildType `dockerfile`.

domains.description:
Domains are extra ingress hosts. The canonical default host is always
attached; a bare custom host is refused here and must go through
add-domain → verify first.

env.description:
Env is the application's environment. Keys must match
`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`; a variable marked `secret: true` is sealed into
KMS and its plaintext is never written to the database.

environment.description: Environment is the deploy target this app names ("production" by default).

image.description: Image is the container image to run, for source `image`.

name.description:
Name is the application's display name. Required; the slug is derived from
it when none is given.

port.description: Port is the container port the app listens on.

project.description: Project is the project to create the application under, from the path.

replicas.description:
Replicas is how many copies to run; clamped to the deployment's limit
rather than refused.

repo.description: Repo is the git source to build from, for source `git`.

slug.description:
Slug is the app's identity in the cluster — its CR name and part of its
host. Given or derived from Name, it must match
`^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$`, and one already used in this
project is 409.

source.description:
Source is `git`, which requires repo.url, or `image`, which requires
image.repository. Anything else is 400.

storageGb.description:
StorageGB is the persistent volume size in GiB; absent means stateless.
Clamped to the deployment's limit rather than refused.

exposureEvent.description:
ExposureEvent is the event that marks a subject as enrolled — the analysis
denominator — defaulting to the SDK's $feature_flag_called marker.

flagKey.description:
FlagKey names the assignment flag this experiment writes, defaulting to
exp_<id>. It must be a slug.

id.description:
ID is the experiment's slug, claimed once per project. It must match
[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}.

metricEvent.description:
MetricEvent is the event that counts as a conversion — the analysis
numerator.

name.description: Name is free text for a reader; the id is what addresses the experiment.

subjectKind.description:
SubjectKind is the unit assigned and measured: user (the default), org,
session or audience.

variants.description:
Arms are the arms, at least two. Weights that are all zero become an
even split; otherwise they must sum to 100, and at most one arm may be
flagged control.

name.description: Name is the cluster's name. Required.

nodePool.description:
NodePool is the ONE pool the cluster is born with — a cluster with no nodes
runs nothing, so it is not optional. More pools are added afterwards through
POST /v1/visor/clusters/:clusterId/pools.

region.description: Region is the provider region slug (e.g. "nyc3"). Required.

version.description: Version is the Kubernetes version slug; empty takes the provider default.
