description.description: Description is a free-text label for the console. Optional, clipped to 1024 bytes.

events.description:
Events are NATS subject patterns to subscribe to (e.g. "commerce.order.>").
An empty or omitted list means EVERY event on the platform bus. Max 64
patterns, each max 256 bytes.

status.description:
Status is "active" or "disabled". Empty defaults to active. A disabled
endpoint receives no bus deliveries, but can still be exercised with
POST /v1/webhook/{id}/test.

url.description:
URL is the https:// address each matching event is POSTed to. Required,
max 2048 bytes; http:// and every other scheme is refused, because a
webhook carries signed event data and must not travel in the clear.

displayName.description: DisplayName names the flow's initial draft version.

externalId.description: ExternalID is the caller's own id for this flow. Optional.

folderId.description: FolderID groups the flow in the builder's tree. Optional.

trigger.description:
Trigger is the root of the step tree — how the flow starts, and the action
chain that follows. Optional: a flow may be created empty and edited later.

code.description:
Code is an optional vanity code; it must be free across the whole
directory, and omitting it mints a random one. Body-only.

label.description:
Label is cosmetic — trimmed, stripped of control characters, capped — and
never part of a code. Body-only: the URL cannot supply it.

description.description: Description is a free-form blurb, max 4KiB.

name.description:
Name is the repo's handle, unique within the scope, and the last segment of
both clone URLs. Must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$; a trailing
".git" is stripped first. Required.

project.description:
Project narrows the repo to a sub-scope of the org. Omit it to use the
caller's own X-Project-Id scope; it can never widen past the caller's org.

public.description:
Public grants ANONYMOUS read (fetch) only; push and the whole control plane
stay org-authed. Defaults to false.

authHeader.description:
AuthHeader is the request header the credential is injected into, e.g.
"Authorization". Empty means the server needs no credential.

listing.description:
Listing enables a CATALOG entry instead — the id from GET /v1/tools/catalog.
The endpoint is the listing's own streamable-http remote, so a listing that
only ships a stdio package is refused: there is nothing to reach yet.

name.description:
Name labels the server for the org. Required with URL; with Listing it
defaults to the listing's own title.

secret.description:
Secret is the credential VALUE. It is sealed into KMS under a per-org ref
and never stored in SQLite, never listed, and never returned.

url.description:
URL is the server's JSON-RPC endpoint. It must be an http(s) URL naming a
PUBLIC host: loopback, link-local, private and cloud-metadata addresses are
refused here and again when the dialer connects.

id.description: ID is the flow to add a version to, from the path.

trigger.description:
Trigger is the root of the version's step tree. Optional: a version with no
trigger is created invalid, and cannot run until one is set.

accountId.description:
AccountID is the account this wallet belongs to. Required, and it must be
an account of the caller's own org — an unknown one is a 404.

agent.description:
Agent optionally narrows the wallet to one agent within the org. It becomes
a segment of the key ref, so it must be a url-safe segment with no slash.

chain.description:
Chain is the EVM chain this wallet is for, as "eip155:<n>" or a bare
decimal chain id. Optional; a Safe defaults to the Hanzo L1 (36963).

custody.description:
Custody selects the signing backend: "kms" (in-process, always available),
"mpc" or "treasury" (the deployed MPC ring), or "safe" (a Safe smart wallet
owned by an MPC key). Empty uses the deployment's default. A backend that is
not configured fails CLOSED with 503 rather than fabricating a signature.

name.description: Name is the wallet's display label. Optional.

tier.description:
Tier is the MPC wallet tier: hot, warm, cold, gas, bridge, contract_admin,
validator, quarantine or disaster_recovery. Empty defaults to hot.

accountId.description: AccountID scopes the credential where the provider's Verify needs one.

label.description: Label names this connection; empty means "default".

oauth.description:
OAuth is a bundle the CLI already obtained through its own local PKCE flow.
Present ⇒ the Adopt path; absent ⇒ the Token path.

provider.description: Provider is the user-scoped provider's registry id, from the path.

token.description:
Token is the customer-held credential for the Verify path. Read on STDIN by
the CLI, never argv; never logged, echoed, or stored outside KMS.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is what the payer intends to send, for the record. Optional —
the credit is what actually arrives, never what was announced.

chain.description: Chain is the network to receive on. Empty takes the rail's default.

token.description: Token is the asset on that chain. Empty takes the chain's native one.

featured.description: Featured puts the listing on the front of the shelf, or takes it off.

hidden.description: Hidden takes the listing off the org-visible shelf, or puts it back.

id.description: ID is the listing to curate, from the path.

logo.description:
Logo is the brand mark to render, an https URL. Empty clears ours and lets
the next sync adopt the publisher's own icon again.

official.description:
Official overrides the derivation: setting it makes this answer FINAL, so
no later sync re-derives over it. That is the difference between a default
and a decision — the derivation can only tell that a domain-verified
publisher serves the endpoint, not that the product is theirs.

name.description: Name is the database name to create.

documentId.description:
DocumentId is the document to attach. Required, and it must already exist
in the caller's own store — this route attaches, it never uploads.

id.description:
ID is the room to add to. It is the path segment: the URL is the addressing
authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the caller's principal,
so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

orderIndex.description:
OrderIndex fixes the document's place in the viewer's list. Optional; a
number or a numeric string is accepted, and anything that is not a number
leaves the document unordered, which sorts it last.

description.description:
Description is the room's description. Optional; any JSON scalar is
accepted and stored as its text, and omitting it leaves the room with none.

name.description:
Name is the room's display name. Required, and a room without one is
refused with the data room's own validation error.

allowDownload.description:
AllowDownload permits downloading rather than viewing only. Optional and
OFF by default; any truthy JSON value turns it on.

allowList.description:
AllowList narrows which addresses pass the email gate. Optional; an entry
may be a full address ("ada@example.com"), an "@domain.com" suffix, or a
bare "domain.com". An omitted or EMPTY list admits everyone, so a link with
no list enforces the email gate alone.

dataroomId.description:
DataroomId is the room to share. One of dataroomId or documentId is
required, and the target must exist in the caller's own store.

denyList.description:
DenyList rejects addresses, in the same three forms as the allow list.
Optional. It is checked BEFORE the allow list, so deny always wins.

documentId.description:
DocumentId shares a SINGLE document instead of a room. One of dataroomId or
documentId is required.

emailProtected.description:
EmailProtected makes a visitor state an address before entering. Optional
and ON by default: it is disabled only by the JSON literal false, so any
other value — including the string "false" — leaves the gate on.

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt closes the link, in unix milliseconds. Optional; a number or a
numeric string is accepted, and omitting it means the link never expires.

name.description: Name labels the link. Optional; any JSON scalar is stored as its text.

password.description:
Password gates the link. Optional; it is hashed with bcrypt before storage
and is never readable back through any route.

description.description: Description is free text about what this set measures; over 64 KiB is refused.

metadata.description: Metadata is a free-form object stored with the set and echoed back verbatim.

name.description:
Name is the dataset's org-unique handle and the segment that will address
it, so it must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$.

winner.description:
Winner is the variant to promote. It must name one of this experiment's own
arms.

email.description: Email identifies the founder on the formation.

status.description: Status is the decision: reviewer_confirmed or failed. Nothing else is accepted.

code.description: Code is the source to run, capped so one function cannot amplify the store.

envNames.description:
EnvNames are the secret NAMES to mount. Values live in the secret store and
are never carried here.

environment.description:
Environment is a second spelling of runtime, accepted so a console that says
"environment" needs no translation.

handler.description: Handler is the entry point within the code.

image.description: Image names a prebuilt image to run instead of source.

memoryLimit.description:
MemoryLimit is the memory the function runs with, defaulting to 256Mi. It is
also the multiplier on the GB-seconds compute charge.

name.description:
Name is the function's org-unique handle and the segment that addresses it,
matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. The names that would shadow a
collection route are reserved.

namespace.description:
Namespace groups functions for display. It is cosmetic — the org is the
isolation key — and is normalised to a DNS-safe label.

runtime.description: Runtime is the language the code runs under: node, python or deno.

target.description:
Target is where the function runs: sandbox (the default) or fleet, the org's
own GPU fleet. fleet supports runtime=python only.

timeoutSec.description:
TimeoutSec is the per-invocation deadline, defaulting to 30 and clamped at
900 — a larger value is capped rather than reset to the default.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

commit.description:
Commit is the git commit or ref to build, for a git-source app. Defaults to
the app's branch.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

tag.description:
Tag is the image tag to deploy, for an image-source app. Defaults to the
app's tag, then `latest`.

project.description: Project is the deployed project's id. Required.

repoUrl.description:
RepoURL is the source repository the project was built from. Empty means a
hand-built project with nothing to attribute — an honest no-op, not an error.

label.description:
Label names this connection so one user can hold several per provider
("work", "personal"). Empty means "default". 1-64 of [A-Za-z0-9._-].

provider.description: Provider is the user-scoped provider's registry id, from the path.

name.description: Name is the custom domain to attach, e.g. "www.acme.com".

project.description: Project is the Pages project name, from the path.

name.description:
Name is the drive's name, matching the same shape a space name does. It
becomes the FIRST SEGMENT of every key the drive holds, which is why it may
carry no "/".

space.description:
Space is the space to create the drive in, from the path. It carries NO
`url:"-"`, unlike the field below it, and the difference is the whole reason
both tags are written out: zip's binder skips a field tagged "-" for EVERY
URL source, path params included, so a path-borne value that carried it
would arrive empty and the create would refuse a perfectly good address.

expedited.description:
Expedited asks for prioritised handling. Only meaningful when the
responsible party cannot file online.

naics.description: NAICS is the six-digit code for what the business does.

responsible.description: Responsible is the person the IRS holds answerable for the entity.

id.description: ID is the item within that namespace.

kind.description: Kind is the item's namespace: "model", "provider" or "feature".

connector.description: Connector names the stored credential to reach this endpoint with.

locator.description:
Locator addresses the resource. For a git source it is the https clone URL on
the provider's own host, with no embedded credentials; for a native target it
is the repository name.

provider.description:
Provider is the platform: github or gitlab for a source; a target defaults to
the native Hanzo Git plane.

account.description: Account is the provider-side account identifier.

host.description: Host is the machine's human hostname label.

kind.description:
Kind decides how the account's inference BILLS and defaults to
subscription: a subscription account bills the user's own monthly plan and
is metered here for visibility only, while an apikey account bills through
commerce on the gateway path.

machine.description: Machine is the stable machine identifier. Required, length-bounded.

os.description: OS is the machine's operating system label.

plan.description: Plan is the provider plan label (e.g. "Claude Max").

provider.description: Provider is the AI provider the account belongs to. Required, length-bounded.

usage.description:
Usage is an optional usage snapshot, clamped and re-serialized to known
fields; omitting it keeps the last good one.

signed.description:
Signed, when present, overrides what the provider reports — the manual path
for a provider whose webhook is not wired. Omit it to take the provider's answer.

fieldMeta.description:
FieldMeta is your own metadata for this field — a label, a placeholder, a
required flag — stored verbatim and handed back on every read of the
document. Any JSON, and esign never interprets it.

height.description:
Height is the field's height, defaulting to -1, which means the renderer
chooses one when the document is sealed.

page.description: Page is the 1-based page the field sits on, defaulting to 1.

positionX.description: PositionX is the field's horizontal position on that page, defaulting to 0.

positionY.description: PositionY is the field's vertical position on that page, defaulting to 0.

recipientId.description:
RecipientID is who must fill this field. Required, and it must belong to this
document — a recipient from elsewhere is refused rather than silently
accepted.

type.description:
Type is what the field collects: SIGNATURE, FREE_SIGNATURE, INITIALS, NAME,
EMAIL, DATE, TEXT, NUMBER, RADIO, CHECKBOX or DROPDOWN. Required, and
anything else is refused.

width.description:
Width is the field's width, defaulting to -1, which means the renderer
chooses one when the document is sealed.

email.description:
Email is where the signing link is meant to go, lower-cased on the way in.
Required.

name.description:
Name is the recipient's display name, also the fallback a NAME field is
filled with when they leave it blank. Optional.

role.description:
Role is SIGNER (the default), CC, VIEWER, APPROVER or ASSISTANT; anything
else reads as SIGNER. A CC recipient is recorded as already complete, because
they are never asked to sign. SIGNER and APPROVER are the roles a document
waits for before it can seal.

signingOrder.description:
SigningOrder is this recipient's position when the document is SEQUENTIAL —
lower signs first, and ties fall back to the order they were added. Ignored
by a PARALLEL document. Optional.

reason.description:
Reason is why the signer is declining. Optional, stored, and written onto the
audit trail with the rejection — it is what the sender sees.

externalId.description:
ExternalID is your own identifier for this document, stored and echoed back
so a document here can be matched to a record in your system. Optional.

message.description:
Message is the covering message carried with the document. Optional, and like
the subject it is stored rather than sent.

pdfBase64.description:
PdfBase64 is the document itself, base64-encoded; a `data:` URL prefix is
accepted and stripped. Required. The bytes go to object storage rather than
into the tenant database, and this ORIGINAL is kept under its own key so it
survives sealing untouched.

signingOrder.description:
SigningOrder chooses PARALLEL — the default, where everyone may sign at once
— or SEQUENTIAL, where each signer waits for the ones ahead of them. Anything
else reads as PARALLEL, and the choice is fixed for the document's life.

subject.description:
Subject is the covering subject line carried with the document. Optional, and
nothing in this surface emails it — delivering the signing links is the
caller's.

title.description:
Title is the document's name, shown to every recipient and used to build the
download filename. Required — a request without one is refused and nothing is
stored.

isBase64.description:
IsBase64 marks Value as drawn signature image bytes rather than a typed
signature. Only a signature field reads it, and a `data:` URL prefix is
stripped.

value.description:
Value is what goes in the field. A signature takes the drawn image bytes or a
typed name; a DATE, NAME or EMAIL field falls back to today, the recipient's
name or their email when this is omitted; every other type requires it.

distinct_id.description: DistinctID is the identity the flags are evaluated for. Required.

groups.description: Groups are the group-level properties, keyed by group type index.

person_properties.description: PersonProperties are the person-level properties conditions match against.

criteria.description: Criteria is the written standard the judge applies; over 64 KiB is refused.

model.description: Model is the model that will do the grading.

name.description:
Name is the judge's org-unique handle, matching
^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. Re-posting a name edits that judge
rather than adding a second one.

scoreName.description:
ScoreName is the name the resulting scores are filed under. It defaults to
the judge's own name and must match the same pattern.

actor.description:
Actor is who produced the turn. Empty takes the validated caller, which is
what an agent writing its own transcript wants; naming one is for a surface
recording on somebody else's behalf.

id.description: ID is the session to append to, from the path.

kind.description:
Kind is what this turn IS: message, tool-call, spawn, log, status, control
or progress. Anything else is refused — the vocabulary is closed so a
reader can branch on it.

payload.description:
Payload is the turn's own body, any valid JSON up to 64 KiB. It is SCANNED
for credentials before it is stored, and a hit refuses the whole append with
422 and the findings — this plane never redacts a secret into a transcript
it then keeps.

Its SHAPE is the writer's business for every kind but one: a `progress`
turn is the run reporting on itself in a shape this surface publishes —
{"pct":0-100 (optional), "phase":"running|blocked|done",
"activity":"≤120 chars"} — so a malformed one is refused with 400 instead
of being stored as prose nobody reads.

argv.description:
Argv is the command as an argument vector, which is the honest form: it
cannot be word-split by accident. Send this OR Command, not both.

command.description:
Command is a shell line, for a caller that holds one. It is a convenience
over Argv and is the only input that ever reaches a shell.

dir.description:
Dir is the working directory to run in. Empty runs in the class's own
workdir — /mnt/data for exec, /work for dev.

id.description: ID is the sandbox to run in, from the path.

stdin.description: Stdin is fed to the command on its standard input.

timeoutSec.description: TimeoutSec bounds the run in seconds. Zero takes the default.

content.description:
Content is the file's full text. Max 1 MiB per file; binary files should
simply be omitted rather than sent.

path.description: Path is the file's repo-relative path, e.g. "internal/store/db.go".

documentIds.description:
DocumentIDs are the documents to file. At least one is required, and every
one must belong to the caller's org — a filing can never reach across orgs.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state or agency the filing is for, e.g. "DE".

data.description:
Data is the workflow graph (the product's nodes/edges document),
verbatim. Omit it to create an empty workflow.

description.description: Description says what the workflow does.

name.description:
Name is the workflow's display name, unique within the org's project
(the product de-duplicates by suffixing).

input.description: Input is the run's chat input value, handed to the graph's input node.

session.description:
Session groups runs into one conversation; the product mints one when
absent and returns it in the response.

tweaks.description:
Tweaks override component fields for this run only (the product's
tweaks document), verbatim.

workflow.description: Workflow is the UUID of the workflow to run.

data.description: Data replaces the workflow graph when present, verbatim.

description.description: Description replaces the description when present.

locked.description: Locked freezes or unfreezes the workflow against edits when present.

name.description: Name renames the workflow when present.

workflow.description: Workflow is the workflow's UUID, taken from the path.

founders.description:
Founders is every founding stakeholder. Each needs a name and an email, and
equityBps between 0 and 10000 (1% == 100 bps).

data.description:
Data supplies every merge field the template declares, keyed by field key.
Every declared field is REQUIRED: a missing one is refused with 400 rather
than rendered as a blank into a contract.

templateId.description:
TemplateID is the template to render. Required; resolved for the caller's
org, so an override wins over the built-in.

branch.description: Branch is the branch to build; defaults to `main` for a git source.

url.description:
URL is the repository clone URL. Required for source `git`, and validated
against the same allowlist the privileged build enforces.

state.description:
State is the GitHub issue state to walk: "open" (the default), "closed" or
"all". Anything else is a 400.

accounts.description:
Accounts names GitHub logins the App is installed on ("hanzoai"). Matched
case-insensitively, since GitHub logins are. Ignored when all is true.

all.description: All binds every account the App holds, instead of naming them.

org.description:
Org is the GitHub account to fork INTO; empty forks to the installation's
own account, which is the common case.

repo.description: Repo is a repository the org's installation was GRANTED, by name.

all.description:
All imports every repository the installation grants, instead of naming
them. Archived and disabled repositories are skipped either way — they
cannot be fetched.

repos.description:
Repos names the repositories to import, either owner-qualified
("hanzo-apps/ai") or as a bare name ("ai"); a trailing ".git" is stripped.
A bare name that matches more than one granted repository is an error
rather than a guess, because one Hanzo org may hold several GitHub
installations and a name is only unique within an owner.
Ignored when all is true.

branch.description:
Branch is the legacy source branch; empty defaults to the repo's own default
branch. Ignored when buildType is "workflow".

buildType.description:
BuildType selects the builder: "workflow" builds via GitHub Actions, anything
else builds from the branch source above.

path.description:
Path is the source directory within the branch: "/" (the default) or "/docs".
GitHub allows no others.

repo.description: Repo is the repository, from the :repo path segment.

branch.description: Branch switches the legacy source branch. Empty leaves the source alone.

buildType.description: BuildType switches the builder: "legacy" or "workflow". Empty leaves it.

cname.description:
CNAME is the custom domain. Omit to leave it alone, "" to clear it, or a
valid FQDN to set it.

httpsEnforced.description: HTTPSEnforced toggles GitHub's enforce-HTTPS bit. Omit to leave it alone.

path.description:
Path is the source directory to pair with Branch: "/" (the default) or
"/docs". Read only when Branch is given.

repo.description: Repo is the repository, from the :repo path segment.

limit.description:
Limit caps the answer; 0 takes the default and anything above the ceiling
is clamped rather than refused.

q.description:
Q is GitHub's own search syntax, passed through: "tetris language:go",
"org:hanzoai stars:>10". Passing it through rather than inventing a
vocabulary means one thing to learn, and it is theirs.

assertions.description:
Assertions is the batch. Each member is judged on its own: one refusal
does not discard the rest, because a caller redelivering five facts must
not lose four of them to one malformed fifth.

at.description:
At is when the thing was so, RFC 3339. Required, and refused when it sits
more than five minutes ahead of the server clock — an assertion dated
further out would never mature and would skew every read until it did.

confidence.description:
Confidence in [0,1]. A tie-breaker within the order, never a substitute
for it. Absent is 0, the weakest an assertion can be.

entity.description:
Entity is the thing being described, in the organization's own namespace.
It is not created: an entity exists because something was asserted about it.
Required, 512 bytes at most.

evidence.description:
Evidence points at the record this claim came from, 512 bytes at most. An
assertion without one is admitted and carries no defence.

names.description:
Names says the value is an entity. A walk reads only the edges, so this is
a declaration and never a guess about the value's shape.

relation.description:
Relation is what is being asserted — `depends`, `owner`, `same`, `title`.
It is open: this plane holds no vocabulary of its own. Required, 128 bytes
at most.

seen.description:
Seen is when this assertion became knowable, RFC 3339. Defaults to At and
may not precede it. It is provenance and it decides nothing: the instant
every read uses is derived as the later of Seen and the server's own clock.

source.description:
Source names who asserted. Required, because an assertion nobody is named
for cannot be weighed against one that is. Open text: this plane ranks no
source above another.

value.description:
Value is what the relation points at. When Names is true it is another
entity's key and the assertion is an EDGE; otherwise it is a scalar and
the assertion is a property. 2048 bytes at most, or 512 when it names an
entity.

as_of.description:
AsOf walks the graph as it stood at an instant, RFC 3339. Absent walks it
as it stands now.

depth.description: Depth is how many hops. Absent is one.

direction.description:
Direction is out, in or both. Out follows an edge from its entity to its
value — what the node points at; in follows it the other way — what points
at the node; both is the union of the two, not a third rule. Absent is out.

relation.description:
Relation narrows the walk to one edge relation. Absent follows all. Only
edges are ever followed: an assertion whose value is a scalar is a property
and is never a hop.

seeds.description: Seeds is where the walk starts. At least one.

as_of.description: AsOf is the instant to answer at, RFC 3339. Absent means now.

entity.description: Entity is the thing to answer about. Required.

relation.description:
Relation is the one relation to settle. Required: this answers a single
(entity, relation) pair, never a whole entity at once.

handle.description:
Handle is the public leaderboard display name; empty opts out. Body-only:
the URL cannot supply it.

description.description:
Description is the customer's message. Optional; it becomes the ticket's
description AND the opening entry of its conversation thread. Clipped at
16 KiB.

email.description:
Email is how the support team replies. Required; clipped at 320 characters
(the RFC 5321 maximum). It is recorded as the ticket's customer, and it is
not verified.

priority.description:
Priority is Low, Medium, High or Urgent, case-insensitively. Anything else —
including omitting it — is recorded as Medium rather than refused.

subject.description:
Subject is the one-line summary of the problem. Required; longer than 300
characters is clipped rather than refused.

clientId.description:
ClientId is the OAuth2/OIDC client identifier and the GLOBAL key every
confidential-client resolver authenticates against (store.GetApplicationByClientId,
the mint gates, Basic auth). It MUST be globally unique across ALL owners — a
collision would let one app shadow another at that key. This store persists each
entity as a JSON document in a shared table, so there is no per-field column to
carry a DB UNIQUE index; uniqueness is enforced at the write in
applications.Create/Update (ensureClientIdUnique), exactly as the (owner,name)
natural key is, and store.GetApplicationByClientId resolves admin-preferring as
defense-in-depth.

accessKey.description:
AccessKey (pk-*) is the publishable identifier and lookup index;
AccessSecret (sk-*) is the confidential secret.
AccessSecret IS NOT PERSISTED for a key minted at or after the digest
change: it carries the secret out to its holder once, in the mint response,
and the row keeps only AccessSecretDigest. It stays on the struct because
that one-time reveal is the whole point of minting, and it stays in the
schema because rows written before the change still hold a plaintext secret
that the resolver drains on first use.

accessSecretDigest.description:
AccessSecretDigest is how a presented secret finds its key: the resolver
digests what the caller sent and looks THAT up. It is what lets the row hold
no plaintext and still be found in one indexed read — a salted hash cannot be
looked up by value, which is the reason the plaintext was here.

act.description:
Act is the durable, opt-in grant that lets this key act FOR a user in its
own org — the credential behind as(): presenting it authorizes minting a
short-lived, user-bound token for a member of the key's tenant. Default
false, so a server key mints nothing on anyone's behalf until the grant is
set deliberately — the capability is never inherited by every key. It is
confined at mint time to the key's OWN Owner, and a reserved-org or
SuperAdmin target is refused, so the grant reaches only ordinary members of
the one tenant that holds the key.

createdTime.description:
CreatedTime and UpdatedTime are RFC3339 audit stamps carried as strings
for byte-parity with the v1 row (orm.Model separately tracks CreatedAt /
UpdatedAt as time.Time for the store's own lifecycle).

expireTime.description:
ExpireTime is when the key stops being honored (empty = never). State is
the lifecycle flag ("Active", "test", …); "test" mints test-env
credentials instead of live ones.

owner.description: Owner is the tenant that holds the key; Name is unique within Owner.

scope.description:
Scope is the key's ACCESS CLASS, orthogonal to Type (which names the bound
principal). Empty (the default, "secret") is a full key: a pk- publishable
half AND a confidential sk- half, the sk- authenticating a server-side reader.
KeyScopePublish is a WRITE-ONLY publishable key — a pk- half only, no secret —
that resolves to just an ORG (never a principal) at the ingest endpoint and is safe
to ship in client JS. A missing value on an existing row reads as the default,
so every pre-Scope key is a secret key unchanged.

type.description:
Type is the scope the key is bound to — "Organization", "Application",
"User", or "General" — and Organization / Application / User name the
concrete principal for whichever scope Type selects.

avatar.description:
How the organization appears across Hanzo — the square mark beside its
name — as an image or as one emoji, never both. It is the pair a person
carries (User.Avatar) under the same names, resolved the same way, so a
screen draws a subject without asking which kind of subject it has. Both
halves live on the row: a mark that appears everywhere cannot be kept on
one device. Written through schema.MarkOf; Logo and LogoDark above are a
different thing, the wordmark a login screen draws.

failedSigninLimit.description:
Per-organization signin throttle. Zero means "inherit the application
default"; a non-zero value overrides it. Safe bounds are clamped by the
resource service before persistence.

founder.description:
Founder is the stable storage id of the identity that provisioned this org
(self-service onboarding). It is the resume token that makes provisioning
converge on a backend where each write autocommits independently (no
transaction rollback): after a partial failure that created the org but did
not move the founder in, a retry recognises the org as the founder's own and
completes it, instead of refusing it as "already taken". It also fences the
org to ONE tenant — a different identity can never complete or join it.

orgBalance.description:
Balance fields are read-only mirrors; authoritative balances live in
Commerce (billing.hanzo.ai). Carried for field-complete v1 parity.

model.description:
Authorization model, targets, and decision. AuthzModel carries the v1
`model` column (the named authz model); it is not the Go identifier
`Model` because that name is taken by the embedded orm.Model[Permission]
mixin. The HTTP contract is unchanged — json:"model".

users.description: Subjects the grant is evaluated for.

nonce.description:
Nonce is the OIDC authorize nonce, stored on the code and echoed into the
id_token minted at the exchange (OIDC Core §3.1.3.6) so a relying party
binds the id_token to its own request and detects replay.

publicGrant.description:
PublicGrant records that this grant was established WITHOUT client
authentication — a PKCE code exchange from a client that presented no
secret. Whether a client is confidential is a property of the GRANT, not
only of the registration: `hanzo-cli` and every @hanzo/iam SPA keep a
registered secret for a BACKEND path while the surface that actually signs
in is a public PKCE client that cannot hold one. authorizationCodeGrant
already makes exactly that bounded relaxation; this is the same fact,
recorded so refreshTokenGrant can honour it instead of demanding a secret
the client never had (which 401s invalid_client and kills the session at
the access token's expiry). Carried across rotation, so the second refresh
behaves like the first.

redirectUri.description:
RedirectUri binds the authorization code to the exact redirect URI of the
authorize request (RFC 6749 §4.1.3): the token endpoint refuses a code
redeemed with a different redirect_uri, closing code-injection across a
client's registered URIs.

refreshFamily.description:
Refresh-token rotation state (v2). Each refresh belongs to a family (the
grant); rotation mints a new row in the same family and marks the prior
one consumed. Presenting a consumed refresh is reuse — the whole family is
revoked (RFC 9700 §4.14.2). RefreshExpireIn is the refresh token's own
absolute expiry (unix), independent of the access token's shorter life.

accessKey.description:
API credentials. AccessSecret / AccessSecretHash / the OAuth tokens are
bearer material, so Mask blanks them and the handler's redact() strips them
before responding. They carry real json tags because a field orm never saves
is a field that silently vanishes.

A presented secret is resolved through Key.AccessSecretDigest and nowhere
else, so no credential is ISSUED into these columns: they hold what older
rows left behind, and every writer that touches them clears them.

balance.description:
Balance mirrors v1 for lossless migration but is authoritative in
Commerce (billing.hanzo.ai), not here — do not write it from IAM.

github.description: Linked federated-identity subjects, one column per connector (v1 parity).

id.description:
Id is the user's STABLE OPAQUE identifier — the value the OIDC `sub` claim
carries. It is the v1 the legacy surface per-row UUID (e.g.
"e7d7fda0-4c53-4508-9d35-7ec892b7e5d7"), migrated verbatim so a user's `sub`
is byte-identical across the cutover: every live session, external reference,
and the downstream money-path principal keyed on `sub` survive unchanged. A
user minted natively in v2 is assigned a fresh UUID here on create, so the
`sub` is ALWAYS a stable opaque id going forward — never the (Owner, Name)
pair, which is mutable (a rename would otherwise silently reissue identity).

It is distinct from the embedded orm.Model STORAGE KEY — the value the datastore
locks and looks a row up by — which is NOT (Owner, Name) for every row: a MIGRATED
legacy row is stamped "owner/name" (SetId in the migrator), but a v2-native
users.Create'd row is NOT — Create allocates rather than pinning a key, so its
storage key is a store-assigned surrogate id (a decimal string like
"17847909129933610000001"). (Owner, Name) is therefore the natural/QUERY key
(unique, indexed), not necessarily the storage key: resolve a row for a locked
write by its REAL key (store.GetUserByName(...).Key().Encode(), which stamps both
shapes — see internal/oidc updateUser), never by assuming "owner/name". This Id is
a first-class, indexed DOMAIN field; its json tag "id" dominates the promoted
orm.Model `Id_` (also "id") by shallower depth, so the persisted record's "id" is
this UUID — exactly the v1 shape. A row that carries no Id (a not-yet-assigned
pre-cutover user) falls back to the (Owner, Name) subject at mint; every other
path resolves `sub`→user by Id.

mfaRememberDigest.description:
MfaRememberDigest is the digest of the token held by the ONE browser the
deadline above applies to. Without it the deadline is account-wide and "don't
ask again on this browser" switches the second factor off everywhere. It is a
digest, never the token, so a database dump yields nothing presentable — and it
carries a REAL json tag because orm persists via json.Marshal, so `json:"-"`
would never be stored (the trap PasswordHash documents above); Mask() strips it
from every response instead.

owner.description: Identity / tenancy. (Owner, Name) is the natural key.

passwordHash.description:
Credential material. PasswordHash is a one-way bcrypt digest and is
verify-only. It MUST be persisted (orm serializes the entity to its JSON
data column, so a json:"-" field would never be stored — that silently
broke login), so it carries a real json tag; the users API redact() strips
it (and every other secret) from every response. PasswordType and
PasswordSalt describe the digest scheme so rows hashed under the legacy
argon2id scheme can still be verified and lazily re-hashed to bcrypt.

webauthnCredentials.description:
Multi-factor authentication. TotpSecret and RecoveryCodes are secret
verify-only material — the handler strips them from every response.
WebauthnCredentials is carried as raw JSON here for lossless migration;
the typed passkey model is the sibling WebauthnCredential entity.

attestationFormat.description:
AttestationFormat is the statement format the authenticator attested in
("packed", "apple", "none", …), which is a DIFFERENT value from the
attestation type above. The library reads it back when resolving the FIDO
AppID extension, so a row that dropped it would round-trip a credential the
verifier no longer recognises as the one it stored.

code.description: Code is the one-time code delivered to the account's own address.

oldPassword.description:
OldPassword is the credential being replaced, the proof a signed-in caller
gives instead of a code.

organization.description:
The account being recovered, for a caller who cannot be signed in. Read on
the CODE arm only — a signed-in caller is resolved from its own session or
token, never from these.

password.description:
Password is the new credential. It must satisfy the platform floor and the
organization's own complexity options.

enableCodeSignin.description:
EnableCodeSignin offers sign-in by an emailed or texted one-time code
beside the password. A POINTER for the same reason as IsShared: a plain
bool reads as false on every reconcile that says nothing and would switch
the method off for every app whose caller never mentioned it.

expireInHours.description:
ExpireInHours and RefreshExpireInHours are the application's token
lifetimes. They are the ONLY declarative way to say that a refresh token
must OUTLIVE its access token: with neither stated, oidc.refreshTTL clamps
the refresh lifetime to the access lifetime, so the refresh_token grant the
registration advertises expires at the same instant as the token it was
meant to renew and can never be exercised. `hanzo-cli` sat in exactly that
state — a browser re-login every hour, and a live refresh returning 401.

POINTERS, for the same reason as IsShared: a plain float would read as 0 on
every reconcile that says nothing and reset a deliberate lifetime back to
the default. Nil means "not stated, leave it".

isShared.description:
IsShared declares that this application serves EVERY organization, not only
the one named in Organization. It is the honest description of a brand app —
hanzo-id, hanzo-chat, a brand console — whose customers each live in their own
tenant: self-service onboarding moves a founder OUT of the brand org, so
`user.Owner != app.Organization` is the steady state and the app really does
serve every org. Application.ServesOrg reads it as one of the three ways to
say yes.

A POINTER because omission must PRESERVE. This upsert is the operator's
steady-state reconcile and most callers say nothing about sharing; a plain
bool would read as false on every one of them and silently un-share an app —
the same shape of accident that de-secreted apps through update-application.
Nil means "not stated, leave it"; only an explicit true or false moves it.

public.description:
Public declares a client that CANNOT hold a credential — a browser SPA,
a CLI, a desktop app. It proves itself with PKCE instead, and the token
endpoint treats "no stored secret" as exactly that (token.go: a secret is
verified only when one is stored). Without this flag every upsert minted
a secret, so a public client could never be registered at all and its
browser code->token exchange 401'd `invalid_client` forever.

name.description:
Name addresses the team on update and names it on create; every other
field is content and binds from the BODY, never the URL.

Name is the device's name within the org — a DNS label. The fabric knows
the identity as "<name>.<org>"; every answer here uses the caller's name.

roles.description:
Roles are extra role attributes for the identity, each scoped to the
caller's org on the way in ("k3s-host" is written as "k3s-host.<org>") so
no caller can claim an attribute another tenant's policy selects. A role
of the form "<service>-host" makes this identity a HOST of that published
service — the bind policy from POST /v1/network/services selects exactly
that attribute — and is refused when the org has no such service.

repository.description: Repository is the image repository. Required for source `image`.

tag.description: Tag is the image tag to deploy; `latest` when omitted.

range.description: Range is an optional A1 range within the sheet; empty reads the default range.

spreadsheetId.description: SpreadsheetID is a Google Sheets id. Required.

folderId.description: FolderID is a Google Drive folder id. Required.

filterableAttributes.description:
FilterableAttributes replaces the whole filterable set. Omitted leaves it
unchanged; an empty array clears it.

files.description:
Files is the full set of files to index. Required and non-empty; max 20000
files, 1 MiB per file and 1 GiB in total. Unchanged files are skipped by
content hash, so re-sending the whole tree is cheap.

prune.description:
Prune deletes indexed files that are NOT in this request — which makes the
call a full sync of the repo rather than an upsert. Only pass it when Files
is the complete tree.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository label to index under. Required, max 200 bytes. It is
a stored column value, not a filesystem path.

primaryKey.description:
PrimaryKey is the document field that identifies a row. Optional — the
first write establishes one when it is omitted.

uid.description: UID is the index's name within the org. Required.

filter.description:
Filter narrows the hits, in the dialect's filter syntax: a string, or an
array of strings combined with AND. Only attributes named in the index's
filterableAttributes can be constrained. Left unconstrained here because
the dialect accepts both shapes and naming one would publish an API that
cannot send the other.

limit.description: Limit is how many hits to return. Absent means 20; the ceiling is 1000.

offset.description: Offset is where to start. Absent means 0.

q.description:
Q is the search text. Typos are forgiven. An empty Q matches everything,
which is how a client lists an index by relevance rather than by insertion
order.

samples.description:
Samples is the batch form, up to 256 samples; leave it empty to send one
sample inline on the same fields.

tool.description:
Tool is the registry name of the capability to activate (or deactivate) for
the caller's own org and project. Required.

input.description: Input is what the function is given on stdin. It is opaque to this surface.

assignee.description:
Assignee hands the work to somebody — a person or an agent, by the name
they are known by on the forge. "" TAKES IT OFF whoever holds it, which is
why this is a pointer: absent leaves the holder alone.

It is the other half of `claim`, which that handler already named: a claim
takes work for the CALLER and refuses to name anyone else, because giving
work away is a different act with different authority. This is that act,
and until it existed a board could only be worked by whoever clicked
first — an agent could never be given anything.

description.description: Description rewrites the body.

key.description: Key is the board — the repository name, from the path.

num.description: Num is the issue number on that repository, from the path.

status.description: Status moves the card to another column.

expectedOutput.description:
Expected is the answer a correct model produces, which the judge grades
against, stored as raw JSON exactly as sent, up to 64 KiB.

id.description:
ID makes the write idempotent — re-posting the same id replaces that example
in place. Omit it and one is generated. An id that already exists in a
DIFFERENT dataset is 409 rather than a move.

input.description:
Input is what the model under test will be given, stored as raw JSON exactly
as sent, up to 64 KiB.

metadata.description: Metadata is a free-form object stored with the example.

status.description:
Status is ACTIVE (the default) or ARCHIVED. Only ACTIVE examples are fed to
a run, which is how an example is retired without being deleted.

id.description: ID is the job (activity) id, from the URL path.

reason.description: Reason is recorded on the cancellation; empty records "canceled from console".

run.description:
Run is the run id; empty defaults to the job id, which is what the dispatcher
sets (runId == activityId == prompt_id), so the common case sends no body.

criteria.description:
Criteria is the standard the judge applies, defaulting to a correctness
criterion.

model.description:
Model is the model that grades. It defaults to the model under test, so a
run with no judge named has the model grade itself.

name.description:
Name is the score name the judge's grades are filed under, "llm-judge" by
default. A name that is not a legal handle falls back to that default
rather than being stored as sent.

limit.description:
Limit narrows what the minted key may reach, as `kind:name` entries:
`model:zen5`, `project:acme`, `product:commerce`, or `model:*` for a whole
kind. It only ever NARROWS — a key can never reach further than the person
who minted it — so an unrecognised kind costs availability, never privilege.

Omitted mints an unrestricted key, because that is what every key in the
estate is today and a default that restricted would revoke all of them.

Example: {"type": "secret", "limit": ["model:zen5", "project:acme"]}

type.description:
Type is the key class to act on: "secret" (sk-, session-equivalent, belongs
on a server) or "publishable" (pk-, org-identifying, safe in a browser
bundle). Omitted means secret, which is what every existing caller means.

clientId.description: ClientID is the machine identity's id, as IAM issued it.

clientSecret.description:
ClientSecret is that identity's secret. It is never logged, never echoed,
and never carried in an error.

env.description:
Env is the environment to write under. REQUIRED, with no default: it is
part of the storage key, so a silently defaulted write lands in a bucket
the readers that resolve project, environment and path never look in, and
the stale value keeps being served.

name.description: Name is the secret's name. Required.

path.description: Path is an optional subpath beneath the org root, e.g. "/ci".

value.description:
Value is the secret itself. It is sealed under a fresh per-secret data key
before storage, so plaintext never reaches disk, and it is never echoed
back, logged, or carried in an error.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

value.description: Value is the value, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).

class.description:
Class is what the sandbox is FOR: "exec" for a code-interpreter call,
"dev" for a workspace bound to a project, "desktop" for one with a screen.
It decides the image, the working directory and the isolation.

cluster.description:
Cluster names one of the org's attached clusters to run the sandbox on —
the fleet-local name it was registered under. Empty runs on the home
cluster. The named cluster must carry the sandbox namespace and the
gvisor runtime class; a name the org has not attached is 404.

image.description:
Image overrides the image the class would pick. Honoured only for a caller
the policy admits, and the sandbox that comes back names the image it GOT.

project.description:
Project binds the sandbox to one of the org's projects. Required for a dev
or desktop class, which are single-attach per project; an exec sandbox
carries none.

runtime.description:
Runtime asks for an isolation: runc, gvisor, kata-clh or kata-fc. It is a
REQUEST, not a guarantee — the sandbox that comes back carries the runtime
it was actually given, which is the field to read.

ttlSec.description:
TTLSec is how long the lease runs before the reaper may take it, in
seconds. Zero takes the class's own default.

cpuid.description: CPUID is a CPU/board identifier string.

hostname.description: Hostname is a weak signal, used only as a tiebreaker.

install_id.description: InstallID is a per-install random the agent persists locally on first run.

machine_id.description:
MachineID is a stable per-host id (e.g. /etc/machine-id, IOPlatformUUID,
MachineGuid). Strongest single signal where present.

macs.description: MAC addresses of stable interfaces (order-insensitive; we sort).

signals.description:
Signals is the host material the client agent collected. Which fields
actually participate in the binding is deliberately unspecified — send
everything available and let the server decide.

fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint is a previously-registered device binding value, as returned by
POST /v1/licensing/fingerprint. Leave it empty and pass Signals to bind the
device at issue time instead.

holder.description:
Holder overrides who the token is issued to; defaults to the caller's own
validated subject. It NAMES the token's bearer and grants nothing on its
own — the entitlement checked is always the caller's org's.

product.description: Product is the licensed commerce product the caller wants a token for.

release.description:
Release scopes the token to one signed binary release, recorded as a
"release:<id>" feature so a single bad release can be revoked on its own.

signals.description:
Signals binds the device at issue time, as an alternative to a
pre-registered fingerprint. The raw signals are never stored or echoed —
they are folded immediately into the one-way binding value.

ttl_seconds.description:
TTLSeconds requests a token lifetime in seconds. It is clamped to the
deployment maximum AND to the entitlement's own expiry — a token never
outlives the subscription that paid for it.

app_id.description: AppID scopes the release to an app build ("hanzo" | "lux" | "zoo").

artifact_ref.description: ArtifactRef is where the binary lives (object-store key / OCI ref / path).

cosign_cert.description:
CosignCert is the cosign/Fulcio cert (keyless) or public key ref used to
verify CosignSignature. The download response hands this to the client.

cosign_signature.description: CosignSignature is the base64 cosign signature over the artifact digest.

id.description:
ID is the release identifier, e.g. "engine-rocm-0.4.2-linux-amd64". The
accelerator belongs here — one product is built several ways — and never
in Product below.

min_features.description: MinFeatures, when set, are features the license must include to download.

product.description:
Product is the licensed product this artifact belongs to (commerce SKU):
"engine" for every one of those builds.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the hex digest of the artifact (integrity + cosign subject).

version.description: Version is the semantic version of the binary.

yanked.description:
Yanked marks a pulled release (download refused; tokens may be revoked
release-scoped too).

reason.description:
Reason is the operator's note, echoed back by verify so a support agent can
explain the refusal.

scope.description:
Scope is what the revocation matches on: "nonce" kills one token,
"holder" every token issued to one bearer, "fingerprint" every token bound
to one device, and "release" every token scoped to one binary release.

value.description: Value is the concrete nonce, holder, fingerprint or release id to revoke.

app.description:
App overrides the app_id the token is expected to carry. Leave it empty and
the token's own app_id is used — an online verify is informational, and it
is the ENGINE that enforces the app at boot.

token.description: Token is the license token to check.

state.description: State is the set of issues to walk: "open" (the default), "closed" or "all".

secret.description:
Secret is the signing secret configured on the webhook in Linear. Claiming
again with a new value rotates it.

issue.description: Issue is the issue's identifier (ENG-123) or its id.

stream.description: Stream is the stream name, from the path.

from.description:
From is the number to send FROM, in E.164. It must be one this org holds and it
must be sms-capable.

media.description:
Media are URLs to attach. A message with any is an MMS to the carrier — the
distinction is the carrier's to make, not something the caller declares.

text.description: Text is the message body. It may be empty when Media carries the message.

to.description: To is the number to send to, in E.164.

name.description:
Name is the local repo to mirror into, from the :name path segment. It is
CREATED on first use.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope to land the repo in; empty uses the caller's own,
exactly as a create would.

source.description:
Source is the http(s) git URL to fetch from. The host is SSRF-guarded, and a
credential is sent only if we hold one NAMED FOR that host — so a
tenant-supplied URL to anywhere else fetches anonymously.

host.description:
Host is an optional assertion of the target's hostname. The authoritative
host is the one in URL; a value that disagrees with it is refused.

name.description:
Name is the repo whose advanced refs are pushed downstream, from the :name
path segment.

url.description:
URL is the downstream https git remote. Must be https to an allowlisted
host (github.com / gitlab.com); any embedded credentials are stripped.
Required.

labels.description:
Labels are extra labels to set on the object, merged UNDER the tenancy
labels this plane derives from the validated principal — so a label naming
another org's scope cannot displace the real one.

name.description:
Name is the resource's name: a DNS-1123 label
(^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$), lowercased and trimmed. It is the
name the resource answers to for the life of the caller's org.

spec.description:
Spec is the resource's own spec, passed to Kubernetes unchanged. Required —
an empty spec is 400 rather than an empty resource.

add.description:
Add is the product ids to turn ON. Each must already be an ACTIVE entitlement
of the org's plan, unless the caller is a platform super admin.

remove.description: Remove is the product ids to turn OFF. Disabling is never gated.

title.description: Title is the namespace's display title. Cloudflare mints the id.

description.description: Description becomes the issue body.

key.description: Key is the board — the repository name, from the path.

priority.description: Priority is one of none, urgent, high, medium or low.

status.description:
Status is the board column to open into: backlog, todo, in_progress, done
or canceled. Empty opens into backlog.

title.description:
Title is the one line the card is read by on the board. Blank or whitespace
is refused — an untitled card cannot be told apart from any other.

batch.description: Batch is how many messages to pull (1–1000, default 1).

expires.description: Expires is how long to wait for messages, e.g. "5s" (default "30s", max "60s").

name.description: Name is the consumer name, from the path.

no_wait.description: NoWait answers immediately with whatever is available instead of waiting.

stream.description: Stream is the stream name, from the path.

body.description: Body is the message text, sent verbatim when present — the no-template path.

channel.description:
Channel selects the delivery channel, sms or email. The per-channel routes
(/send/sms, /send/email) pin it, overriding whatever the body names; on the
generic route it is required.

event.description:
Event is the event name, which doubles as the template id when TemplateID is
empty — the IAM OTP path sends event=iam.otp_sent and nothing else.

provider.description:
Provider pins a provider service name (twilio, plivo, twilio_email, mail).
Empty picks the one whose org credentials are actually configured in KMS.

subject.description: Subject is the message subject, carried on the email channel only.

sync.description:
Sync must be exactly "true": delivery here is synchronous, and anything else
answers 503 because the queue plane that would run an async dispatch is owned
elsewhere. Over REST it rides as ?sync=true (the URL binds over the body); a
by-name call states it in its arguments.

template_id.description: TemplateID selects a built-in template when Body is empty.

template_vars.description:
TemplateVars carries the values the selected template renders against, as
a raw JSON object. Raw on purpose: the by-name call plane computes an
input's layout before reading any payload and refuses a map field
outright, which would make every typed call to these ops fail — and that
call is the reason they are typed at all (IAM's OTP sender). deliver
decodes it right before the template renders, so REST bodies decode
byte-identically to the map this replaced.

to.description:
To is the destination address per recipient — a phone number for sms, an
email address for email. Several recipients fan out into one provider call
each, and the response shape follows the count (see the items field).

credentials_ref.description: CredentialsRef is the name of the secret within the secret manager to use as credentials.

password_ref.description: PasswordRef is the name of the secret within the secret manager to use as the password.

username_ref.description: UsernameRef is the name of the secret within the secret manager to use as the username.

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

fillGaps.description: FillGaps is used to fill the gaps in the time series data

unit.description:
Unit for the time series data shown in the graph
This is used in alerts to format the value and threshold

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

force_implicit_tls.description:
ForceImplicitTLS controls whether to use implicit TLS (direct TLS connection).
true: force use of implicit TLS (direct TLS connection)
false: force disable implicit TLS (use explicit TLS/STARTTLS if required)
nil (default): auto-detect based on port (465=implicit, other=explicit) for backward compatibility

expression.description: expression to filter by following the filter syntax

description.description: step description

name.description: step name

deploymentProjectId.description: Project ID where central pub/sub for logs exist

deploymentRegion.description: Project ID where otel collector will be deployed

projectIds.description: List of project IDs to monitor

authorization.description: The HTTP authorization credentials for the targets.

basic_auth.description: The HTTP basic authentication credentials for the targets.

bearer_token.description:
The bearer token for the targets. Deprecated in favour of
Authorization.Credentials.

bearer_token_file.description:
The bearer token file for the targets. Deprecated in favour of
Authorization.CredentialsFile.

enable_http2.description:
EnableHTTP2 specifies whether the client should configure HTTP2.
The omitempty flag is not set, because it would be hidden from the
marshalled configuration when set to false.

follow_redirects.description:
FollowRedirects specifies whether the client should follow HTTP 3xx redirects.
The omitempty flag is not set, because it would be hidden from the
marshalled configuration when set to false.

http_headers.description:
HTTPHeaders specify headers to inject in the requests. Those headers
could be marshalled back to the users.

oauth2.description: The OAuth2 client credentials used to fetch a token for the targets.

tls_config.description: TLSConfig to use to connect to the targets.

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

alert_source_token.description: AlertSourceToken is the key used to authenticate with the alert source in incident.io.

max_alerts.description:
MaxAlerts is the maximum number of alerts to be sent per incident.io message.
Alerts exceeding this threshold will be truncated. Setting this to 0
allows an unlimited number of alerts. Note that if the payload exceeds
incident.io's size limits, you will receive a 429 response and alerts
will not be ingested.

timeout.description:
Timeout is the maximum time allowed to invoke incident.io. Setting this to 0
does not impose a timeout.

url.description: URL to send POST request to.

enable_update.description: EnableUpdate indicates whether this field should be omitted when updating an existing issue.

template.description: Template is the template string used to render the field.

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt is when the key stops working, as a unix timestamp in seconds.
Zero means it never expires; a past timestamp is refused.

name.description:
Name is the key's name: a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters,
digits or hyphens, at most 80 characters. Required.

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt is when the key stops working, as a unix timestamp in seconds.
Zero means it never expires; a past timestamp is refused.

name.description:
Name is the key's new name, under the same rules it was created with.
Required.

query.description: Query is the query text. Required.

queryType.description:
QueryType says which language the query is in — promql or the datastore's
SQL dialect. Required.

excludeStatusCodes.description:
ExcludeStatusCodes are status codes excluded from the score, comma
separated.

serviceName.description: ServiceName is the service the threshold applies to.

threshold.description: Threshold is the satisfied-response time in seconds.

email.description: Email is the key carrying the email; defaults to "email".

groups.description: Groups is the key carrying the group list; defaults to "groups".

name.description: Name is the key carrying the display name; defaults to "name".

role.description: Role is the key carrying the role; defaults to "role".

googleAuthConfig.description: Google is the Google provider's settings, when SSOType is google_auth.

oidcConfig.description: OIDC is the OIDC provider's settings, when SSOType is oidc.

roleMapping.description: RoleMapping maps the provider's groups onto roles for new users.

samlConfig.description: SAML is the SAML provider's settings, when SSOType is saml.

ssoEnabled.description: SSOEnabled turns enforced SSO on for the domain.

ssoType.description: SSOType picks the provider — saml, google_auth or oidc.

invites.description: Invites are the invitations to create; an email may appear only once.

newPassword.description: NewPassword is the password to set.

oldPassword.description:
OldPassword is the current password; the change is refused when it does
not match.

id.description: ID is the dashboard id from the path.

ops.description:
Ops are the JSON Patch operations, applied in order. On the wire this IS the
request body — a bare array, not an object.

from.description: From is the source JSON Pointer for move and copy; ignored otherwise.

op.description: Op is the verb: add, remove, replace, move, copy or test.

path.description:
Path is a JSON Pointer into the postable dashboard, e.g.
/spec/display/name, /spec/panels/<id>, /tags/-.

value.description:
Value is the value to add/replace/test; its type depends on Path. Required
for add, replace and test; ignored otherwise.

generateName.description:
GenerateName derives a fresh unique name from spec.display.name instead of
taking Name.

image.description: Image is an optional cover image reference.

name.description:
Name is the dashboard's unique internal name (a DNS-1123 label). Omit it
with generateName to derive one from the display name.

schemaVersion.description: SchemaVersion is the dashboard schema version; must be the current v6.

spec.description:
Spec is the Perses dashboard spec (display, variables, panels, layouts,
datasources). Its plugin-defined leaves are open JSON, carried verbatim.

tags.description:
Tags are the dashboard's tags; at most ten, and none may use a reserved DSL
key.

key.description: Key is the tag key.

id.description: ID is the dashboard id from the path.

query.description: Query is the variable query to evaluate. Required.

variables.description:
Variables are the current values of the other dashboard variables, for
queries that reference them.

order.description: Order is the captured sort direction.

query.description: Query is the captured filter DSL.

sort.description: Sort is the captured sort field.

version.description: Version is the saved-view schema version; must be v1.

data.description: Data is the listing state the view captures.

name.description: Name is the saved view's name; at most 32 characters, no surrounding space.

id.description: ID is the saved view id from the path.

end.description: End is the window end, as epoch nanoseconds. Required.

start.description: Start is the window start, as epoch nanoseconds. Required.

tags.description: Tags narrow the graph to spans matching every condition.

displayName.description: DisplayName is the new display name; empty leaves it unchanged.

role.description:
Role is the legacy role to move to — ADMIN, EDITOR or VIEWER; empty
leaves it unchanged.

aggregations.description: Aggregations are the measures to compute per group. Empty means a count.

filters.description:
Filters narrow the scan; each is a field, an operator (eq, neq, like) and
a value, and they combine with AND.

groupBy.description: GroupBy are the columns to group the rows by.

limit.description: Limit caps how many rows come back.

orderBy.description: OrderBy is the column or aggregation to sort the rows on.

period.description: Period is the window to read, relative to now — 1h, 24h, 7d, 14d, 30d.

project.description: Project is the project to read, as its id. Required.

description.description: Description describes the field, when known.

fieldContext.description:
FieldContext says which plane the field lives on, e.g. attribute,
resource, span.

fieldDataType.description: FieldDataType is the field's type: string, int64, float64 or bool.

name.description: Name is the field's name. Required.

signal.description: Signal is the telemetry signal the field belongs to, e.g. traces.

unit.description: Unit is the field's unit, when known.

domain.description:
Domain narrows the read to one external domain (the domain view requires
it).

end.description: End is the window's end, epoch milliseconds.

endpoint.description: Endpoint narrows the domain view to one endpoint.

filter.description: Filter is an additional predicate in the query-builder filter syntax.

groupBy.description: GroupBy adds grouping columns to the result.

show_ip.description:
ShowIP keeps rows whose domain is a bare IP address; they are dropped
otherwise.

start.description: Start is the window's start, epoch milliseconds.

end_time.description: EndTime is the end of the window, as a millisecond epoch.

start_time.description: StartTime is the start of the window, as a millisecond epoch.

step_end.description: StepEnd is the step the transition runs to, 1-based.

step_start.description:
StepStart is the step the transition runs from, 1-based. Ignored by the
reads that span the whole funnel.

steps.description: Steps are the funnel's steps, in order. At least two are needed.

email.description: Email is the account's address. Required.

orgId.description: OrgID picks the org to sign into when the address belongs to several.

password.description: Password is the account's password. Required.

assignee.description: Assignee is who the issue is assigned to.

id.description: ID is the issue id.

status.description: Status is the new lifecycle state: unresolved, resolved or ignored.

end.description: End is the window end, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

exceptionType.description: ExceptionType narrows to one exception type.

serviceName.description: ServiceName narrows to one reporting service.

start.description: Start is the window start, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

tags.description: Tags narrow the scan to spans carrying the given tag values.

end.description: End is the window end, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

exceptionType.description: ExceptionType narrows to one exception type.

limit.description: Limit caps how many exception groups come back. Required, non-zero.

offset.description: Offset is how many groups to skip.

order.description: Order is the direction: ascending or descending.

orderParam.description: OrderParam is the column to order by, e.g. exceptionCount, lastSeen.

serviceName.description: ServiceName narrows to one reporting service.

start.description: Start is the window start, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

tags.description: Tags narrow the scan to spans carrying the given tag values.

eventName.description: EventName names the event; required for track events.

eventType.description: EventType is the kind of event — track, identify or group. Required.

rateLimited.description: RateLimited marks an event the reporting client rate-limited.

dataType.description:
DataType is the field's data type, e.g. string, int64, float64, bool.
Required.

index.description:
Index is the index expression to put on the column, e.g. minmax,
set(N), bloom_filter(P), tokenbf_v1(S,H,SEED). Empty keeps the default.

indexGranularity.description: IndexGranularity is the index granularity in rows.

name.description: Name is the field to tune. Required.

selected.description: Selected materializes the field as its own column when true.

type.description: Type is where the field lives: attributes or resources. Required.

field.description: Field is the column to test.

op.description: Op is how to test it: eq, neq or like.

value.description: Value is what to test it against.

dataType.description: DataType is the attribute's value type — string, int64, float64 or bool.

isColumn.description: IsColumn marks an attribute stored as its own column.

isJSON.description: IsJSON marks an attribute read out of a JSON body.

Listed publishes the org on the cross-org global board when true, and withdraws
it when false.

externalId.description: ExternalID sets the caller's own id for this flow.

folderId.description: FolderID moves the flow in the builder's tree.

id.description: ID is the flow to update, from the path.

metadata.description: Metadata replaces the caller's opaque JSON.

publishedVersionId.description:
PublishedVersionID pins the version runs execute. It must name a version OF
THIS FLOW; empty clears the pin, so runs take the latest version again.

name.description: Name is the repo to update, from the :name path segment.

public.description:
Public flips anonymous read access. Omit it and the request is refused —
there is nothing else to update yet.

cwd.description:
Cwd is where the session is working NOW.

It was write-once — captured at register and never again — which is right
for a run that starts in a directory and stays there, and wrong for a linked
shell, which is a place a person moves around in. The console showed the
directory `hanzo link` happened to be run from and kept showing it after the
shell had walked away, so the field answered "which work is this" with an
answer that was true once. A pointer, so an unchanged path is an omitted
field rather than a repeated write.

id.description: ID is the session to update, from the path.

project.description:
Project tags the product this session built; Published is the author's
decision to let anyone read the story (provenance.go). Both are pointers so
"absent" and "cleared" are different requests.

published.description:
Published opens the session's story to the public build route; false withdraws
it, and withdrawing is always allowed. PUBLISHING is refused unless the
session names a Project — the one set in this same request, or the one already
stored — because that route is keyed on (org, project). It widens READ access
to what is already there and grants nothing else.

status.description:
Status moves the session to running, paused, done or error. A session that has
already finished refuses any change with 409 — done and error are monotonic —
and moving INTO one stamps the end time. This is the surface REPORTING what
happened; a control command never writes it.

target.description: Target re-dispatches a session to a run-target (the #48 association). "" detaches.

terminal.description:
Terminal publishes (or, with "", withdraws) the URL this session's live
terminal can be watched at. A pointer so "absent" and "withdrawn" are
different requests: a session that stops sharing must be able to say so.

title.description:
Title rewrites the human line, up to 512 characters — usually because the work
turned out to be something other than what it was opened as.

actor.description:
Actor is the loop-guard identity the sync writes as. Omitted, the stored actor
stands.

direction.description: Direction is both, pull, push or off. Omitted, the stored direction stands.

id.description: ID is the sync to update, from the path.

kind.description: Kind names a different kind of sync, and is refused, for the same reason.

source.description:
Source, Target and Kind are DECLARED HERE IN ORDER TO BE REFUSED.

They are immutable by design — re-pointing a sync is a delete and a create, so
a link can never silently start syncing somewhere else — but an UNDECLARED
field is dropped by the binder before the handler sees it, so a request asking
to repoint answered 200, changed nothing, and said nothing. The operator then
believes a moved repository has been repointed and it has not.

Live: a sync still naming github.com/hanzoai/cloud after the repository moved
to hanzo-inc/cloud failed every reconcile with "Repository not found", and the
PATCH that appeared to fix it did nothing at all. Declaring the fields is what
lets the documented immutability actually answer.
Source names a new upstream, and is refused. Delete this sync and create the
one you want.

target.description: Target names a new native repository, and is refused, for the same reason.

trigger.description: Trigger is webhook, poll or manual. Omitted, the stored trigger stands.

capacity.description: Capacity rewrites the human summary, up to 256 characters. "" clears it.

host.description:
Host re-points the hostname sessions are matched by. Moving it moves the load:
the session counts follow the new name from the next read.

id.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

kind.description: Kind re-files it under laptop | cloud | gpu | cluster | machine.

label.description:
Label renames the machine, up to 128 characters. Empty STRING is refused — a
target with no name is a row nobody can pick out of a fleet.

metrics.description:
Metrics replaces the live sample, and sending one IS A HEARTBEAT: the server
stamps the time and appends the point to the fleet series. Sending an all-zero
sample CLEARS the heartbeat — the machine goes back to having no liveness fact
at all, and its stored status is taken at face value again.

spec.description:
Spec replaces the static capability whole, sanitized and clamped the same way
a register's is.

status.description:
Status sets operator INTENT: online | offline | draining. Draining is how a
machine is taken out of dispatch without ending what is already on it. What
comes back may still read offline, because the heartbeat outranks the intent.

feeds.description:
Feeds is the RSS/Atom feed URLs to read, at most 64. Each must be an
http(s) URL whose host is on the server's allowlist — the SSRF guard is
applied here, at the write, so a stored pipeline can never name a host the
fetcher would refuse. Blank entries are dropped and duplicates collapse.

filters.description:
Filters narrows the merged feed. Terms are trimmed, de-duplicated
case-insensitively, and capped at 64 per axis.

autoScale.description: AutoScale turns the provider's cluster autoscaler on for this pool.

clusterId.description: ClusterID is the cluster to add the pool to, from the URL path.

count.description: Count is how many nodes the pool starts with.

maxNodes.description:
MaxNodes is the ceiling the autoscaler may not grow the pool past, and so the
bound on what this pool can spend. Ignored unless AutoScale is set.

minNodes.description:
MinNodes is the floor the autoscaler may not shrink the pool below. Ignored
unless AutoScale is set.

name.description: Name is the pool's name.

provider.description:
Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on (e.g. "digitalocean"). Required —
Visor routes the create by it. Accepted from the body or ?provider=.

size.description: Size is the provider size slug for each node (e.g. "s-4vcpu-8gb").

clusterId.description: ClusterID is the cluster holding the pool, from the URL path.

count.description:
Count is the node count to scale TO — an absolute target, not a delta, and
never negative.
