poolId.description:
PoolID is the pool to resize, from the URL path — the `poolId` a cluster read
reports for it. Required.

provider.description: Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on. Required; body or ?provider=.

app.description: App is the parent application's slug, from the path.

branch.description: Branch is the branch to preview; defaults to the parent app's branch.

image.description:
Image is the already-built image ref to deploy. Required — a preview never
builds.

project.description: Project is the project the parent application lives under, from the path.

brief.description:
Brief is what the site should be, in plain language. It is the whole input the
model gets and it is size-bounded.

model.description:
Model names which model writes the site. Absent takes the deployment's
default — this route spends inference on the caller's org either way.

name.description: Name is the site's display name. Taken from what the model writes when omitted.

slug.description:
Slug is the handle and public host label to publish under. Derived from the
name, or from the brief, when omitted.

bytes.description: Bytes is their total size in bytes.

commit.description: Commit is the revision that was built, recorded on the deployment.

files.description: Files is how many objects CI published.

id.description: ID is the queued deployment to complete, from the path.

keys.description:
Keys is the manifest CI just uploaded, RELATIVE to the deployment prefix. It
is what replaces `aws s3 sync --delete`: an upload grant authorizes writes
only, so CI cannot remove a file, and cloud reconciles the prefix against
this list instead (grant.go). Omit it and nothing is deleted — the prefix
only grows, which is the old pre-grant behaviour and a safe default.

liveUrl.description:
LiveURL is a HINT at the address the site should serve at. The public host is
claimed by cloud first, so this can refine the URL a deployment reports but
can never assert a subdomain another tenant holds.

message.description: Message is what happened, in words — on an error completion, why it failed.

slug.description: Slug is the project the deployment belongs to, from the path.

status.description:
Status is how the build ended: `live` if it succeeded, `error` if it did not.
Nothing else is accepted.

analytics.description:
Analytics is the opt-OUT for the wired-by-default analytics beacon: absent
(nil) ⇒ ON (the default); explicit false ⇒ off. A pointer so "unset" is
distinguishable from "false" — the only way to turn the default off.

description.description:
Description is the one-line summary, copied onto anything forked from this
project.

framework.description:
Framework is a BUILD HINT from a closed set, defaulting to static. It tells CI
how to build a linked repo and never gates a deploy.

license.description: License is the terms that upstream work carries.

name.description:
Name is the project's display name and the only REQUIRED field. When slug is
omitted it is also what the slug is derived from.

repo.description:
Repo links a git source, so pushes to it rebuild this project. Omit it for a
project deployed by uploading an artifact.

slug.description:
Slug is the handle everything else addresses this project by: the public host
`<slug>.hanzo.app`, the object-store key segment, and the path parameter of
every later call. Derived from the name when omitted. It is a hostname label,
so it is constrained and reserved labels such as `api` or `admin` are refused.

upstream.description:
Upstream credits the third-party work this project was published from. It is
accepted from any caller: giving away credit can only cost the publisher, so
it needs no gate.

visibility.description:
Visibility is "public" (the default when absent) or "private". Publishing
publicly is ungated — that is the point of a community. Going PRIVATE is
the paid feature, so an unfunded org asking for it is refused rather than
silently downgraded (see resolve).

files.description:
Files is the whole site, inline — every file it consists of. It REPLACES what
is there rather than merging, so an omitted file is a deleted one.

name.description: Name is the site's display name.

slug.description: Slug is the handle and public host label to publish under.

commit.description:
Commit is the git sha this build was produced from, recorded on the
deployment so a released site can be traced back to its source. Optional.

It is the ONLY field here, and deliberately: the predecessor also accepted
`source` and `branch`. `source` was the Content-Type discriminator this
split removed. `branch` was accepted and DISCARDED — there is no branch
column on a deployment, and the lifecycle event derives the branch from the
project's own linked one — so declaring it would publish a settable field
that does nothing into the document, every generated SDK and the MCP input
schema. A field that is read by nothing is not described as if it were.

`url:"-"` because zip binds the query string OVER a decoded body, so
without it a `?commit=` the caller never sent would outrank the one it did.

slug.description: Slug is the site to deploy, from the path.

domains.description:
Domains are the custom hostnames to attach, in order. An empty list is a
400 rather than a clear — releasing a host is its own call.

slug.description: Slug is the site the hosts attach to, from the path.

content.description:
Content is the file's whole text, inline. There is no upload step and no
reference to fetch: a site is sent as its bytes, and each file and the site as
a whole are size-bounded.

path.description:
Path is where the file lands in the site, RELATIVE to its root — so
"index.html" is the page served at /. Leading slashes and any attempt to
escape the root are refused.

name.description: target project name (optional; defaults to the parent's title)

slug.description: parent slug to fork — catalog template or published project (required)

target.description:
Target overrides the derived project slug (optional; defaults to the
parent slug). Kept distinct from Slug so callers can rename on fork.

variant.description:
Variant picks a template's format/page/theme (optional; defaults to the
template's first shape). This is the axis the catalog used to spend
sibling slugs on, so it is expressed here, where the user's preference is.

slug.description: Slug is the site to publish, from the path.

source.description:
Source is the build output to promote, as a path RELATIVE to your org's own
storage space — never a URL and never a bucket. The org segment is prepended
server-side from the validated principal, so the worst a hostile source can
address is something your own org already owns.

cacheControl.description:
CacheControl replaces the Cache-Control policy the edge serves this site's
HTML under. Absent leaves it.

description.description: Description replaces the one-line summary. Absent leaves it.

framework.description:
Framework replaces the build hint. It affects the NEXT build only — nothing
already deployed is rebuilt.

hidden.description:
Hidden is MODERATION, and the only admin-gated field on this body: it pulls
a public project out of the catalogue from admin.hanzo.ai without editing
the publisher's own visibility choice, so un-hiding restores exactly what
they asked for. A tenant sending it is ignored.

hiddenReason.description:
HiddenReason records WHY moderation hid it, so the action can be explained
and reviewed later. Admin-gated like hidden itself.

license.description:
License is the terms that upstream work carries, with the same clear-versus-
leave rule.

name.description: Name replaces the display name. Absent leaves it; the slug never moves with it.

repo.description: Repo relinks the git source. Absent leaves the existing link.

slug.description:
Slug is the project to update, from the path. The URL is the addressing
authority — a `slug` in the body cannot move the write to another project.

tags.description:
Tags sets the site's browser tag config: platform slug → non-secret pixel id
(e.g. {"ga4":"G-…","meta":"…"}). track.js injects these first-party and the
server CAPI reads them, per site. Absent LEAVES them; a present object REPLACES
the set (send {} to clear). The ids are public — they ship in the page — so this
is not the SECRET path (a CAPI token is sealed via POST /v1/destination).

upstream.description:
Upstream credits the third-party work this project was published from, and is
settable after the fact because the live demos are the ones that most need
crediting. An explicit empty string CLEARS the credit; absent leaves it.

visibility.description:
Visibility flips an existing project between "public" and "private". Same
ONE rule as at create: public is free, private needs a paid plan.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

deploymentId.description:
DeploymentID promotes that deployment's exact built image. One of this and
Tag is required.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

tag.description: Tag promotes an image tag, resolved the same way a deploy resolves one.

labels.description: Labels is free-form taxonomy, each up to 64 characters, capped at 32 entries.

name.description:
Name is the org-unique handle AND the URL segment the prompt is addressed by:
1-64 characters matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$. "metrics", "new" and
"catalog" are reserved. A name that already exists appends a new version.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the template body, capped at 64 KiB. It holds template text only —
never a secret.

tags.description: Tags is free-form taxonomy under the same bounds as Labels.

type.description: Type labels the template's kind; defaults to "text".

instance.description:
Instance binds a DEDICATED add-on to the app instance whose
<instance>-addons Secret receives the <KIND>_URL (e.g. "commerce").
Optional: empty means "not instance-bound" — the DSN is returned once and
wired by the caller.

name.description:
Name is the org-unique slug for the new resource, matching
^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$. Every physical name derives from it.

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

description.description: Description is the browse-card blurb, max 4096 characters.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

framework.description: Framework is the stack the kit is built on ("Next.js 14").

preview.description: Preview is the still image the browse card renders, max 4096 characters.

slug.description: Slug is the kit's identity — lowercase alphanumeric with dashes, max 40.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

category.description: Category groups the listing in the shop window.

description.description: Description is the long copy, clipped at 4096 characters.

price.description:
Price is the per-call price as a decimal USD string, exact to 18 places —
"0.0025" is a quarter of a cent and stays one. Empty or "0" (the default)
publishes it free; any positive price makes the listing monetized and
requires Recipient.

public.description: Public makes the listing discoverable by other orgs. Private otherwise.

recipient.description:
Recipient is the seller's payout wallet ID, in the publishing org — the
wallet x402 pays. Required for a monetized listing.

title.description: Title is the shop-window name, 1-200 characters. Required.

tool.description:
Tool is the registry name of the capability being offered. It must already
resolve in the publisher's own scope — there are no phantom listings.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the canonical test id the claim is about, from /catalog.

model.description: Model is the system the score is claimed for.

protocol.description:
Protocol records HOW it was scored — provider-reported, agentic,
third-party-leaderboard — because a provider card and a third party running
its own harness are different kinds of number and must not be blended.

provider.description:
Provider is who the claim belongs to — the lab or leaderboard whose number
this is. It joins a claim to the attempts measured for that same model.

score.description: Score is the reported aggregate, as a percentage.

source.description:
Source is the citation the row was read from. A claim without one is a
number nobody can check, so every write requires it.

files.description: Files purges exactly the listed URLs — at most 30, Cloudflare's per-request cap.

purge_everything.description: Everything drops the zone's entire edge cache.

zone.description: Zone is the 32-hex Cloudflare zone id, from the path.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, carried per Encoding.

path.description: Path is repo-relative. Absolute or traversing paths are refused.

branch.description:
Branch to advance; empty means "main". A fresh branch that is the repo's
first also becomes HEAD.

files.description:
Files are added to or overwritten on the branch tip — files already there
and not listed SURVIVE. At least one, at most 5000, 32 MiB each.

message.description: Message is the commit message; empty gets a generated one.

name.description:
Name is the repo to push into, from the :name path segment. It is CREATED
on first push if it does not exist.

by.description: By is who is recording them — a person, or the importer's name.

data.description:
Data is the claims to record. One row is a correction; many is an import.
There is no separate bulk endpoint because there is no separate operation:
importing a leaderboard and fixing one number are the same write.

account.description: Account is the provider-side account the sample belongs to.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the window's cached-prompt-token count.

confidence.description: Confidence says how real the counters are, as the meter graded itself.

costCents.description: CostCents is the window's spend in cents, as the provider's meter states it.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the window's spend cap in cents, when the meter knows one.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO currency the cost fields are stated in.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is the window's prompt-token count.

kind.description: Kind is subscription or apikey; anything else is refused.

lane.description: Lane names the meter's own lane label for this measurement.

machine.description: Machine is the machine the collector observed the account on. Required.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is the window's completion-token count.

plan.description: Plan is the provider plan label the account is on.

provider.description: Provider is the AI provider whose meter reported this sample. Required.

requests.description: Requests is the window's request count.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when the window resets, RFC 3339, bounded.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a sample the collector derived rather than observed.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total token count.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, clamped 0..100.

window.description:
Window is the window class, one of 6h, day, week, month; anything else is
refused rather than silently reclassified.

windowMinutes.description: WindowMinutes is the window's length as the meter reported it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC 3339, bounded to a
sane interval around now.

room.description:
Room is the LiveKit room, named the way the office client names one
(`<space>_<name>_<id>`). Its leading segment is what binds the room to a
tenant, and it is the segment the caller's membership is checked against.

publicKey.description:
PublicKey is one OpenSSH authorized-key line ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA… you@host").
Required; a line that does not parse is refused and never stored.

title.description:
Title labels the key in the console. Max 256 chars; when omitted the
comment on the key line is used.

account.description:
Account is which subscription or API account under that provider served the
run, up to 256 characters. It is what lets a revoke of that login stop exactly
the sessions it was paying for.

actor.description:
Actor is the "org/sub" identity to record the session under, up to 256
characters. Omit it and the calling principal is used, which is almost always
what you want: it is what a login revoke matches on to stop this session.

agent.description:
Agent is the label the surface opening this session calls itself by
("hanzo-dev"). REQUIRED, up to 128 characters, and free text — nothing
resolves it against a defined agent.

cwd.description:
Cwd is the directory the session starts in, up to 1024 characters. It can be
moved later, because a linked shell walks around.

host.description: Execution context — where this session runs (all optional).

parentSessionId.description:
ParentSessionID makes this a subagent of that session: it inherits the
parent's root, so one flow stays one tree. The parent must exist IN THE SAME
ORG — a foreign or unknown id is a 400, never a tree across tenants. Empty
opens a root session.

project.description:
The readable build (provenance.go): which product this session builds, and
whether its story may be read by the world.

provider.description: Account tag — the linked AI account this session ran under (login manager).

published.description:
Published opens this session's story to the public build route. It is refused
without a Project, because that route is keyed on (org, project) — a build
with no product is not a story anyone can open. False keeps it org-only.

repo.description:
Repo is the code being worked on, up to 512 characters. A label the surface
states; nothing resolves it against the forge.

room.description:
Room is the collaborative room this run was started in (HIP-0523), so a
space view can list the sessions of one room. It is PROVENANCE and is set
only here: there is deliberately no way to move a session to another room, so
it is absent from the patch input and from UpdateSession's SET list.

status.description:
Status opens the session in one of running, paused, done or error. Empty means
running. A TERMINAL status here (done, error) records a session that has
already finished — its end time is stamped now — and nothing can move it
afterwards.

target.description:
Target names a run-target the org has registered. Unlike Host and Repo it IS
resolved: a target that does not exist in this org is a 400, so a session can
never claim to run on another tenant's machine. Empty names no machine.

taskRunId.description:
TaskRunID is that workflow's particular run, same bound. Recorded, not
resolved: this surface does not check the workflow exists.

taskWorkflowId.description:
TaskWorkflowID links this session to the hanzoai/tasks workflow that executes
it, up to 256 characters. Set it and control commands are forwarded to that
engine; leave it and the running surface polls for them instead.

terminal.description:
Terminal is the URL this session's live terminal is published at, so the
console can watch it. Optional — a session that publishes nothing is still
a session.

title.description:
Title is the human line a card shows, up to 512 characters. Optional, and
changeable later.

image.description: Image is the repository name inside the org's namespace (e.g. "cloud").

domain.description: Domain is the name to extend. It is required, and the caller's org must hold it.

years.description: Years is how much longer to hold it, defaulting to 1.

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

description.description: Description is the browse-card blurb, max 4096 characters.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

framework.description: Framework is the stack the kit is built on ("Next.js 14").

preview.description: Preview is the still image the browse card renders, max 4096 characters.

slug.description: Slug is the kit to replace, from the path.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required on every sample.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

provider.description:
Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required
on every sample.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339.

samples.description:
Samples is the batch form: every lane a poller measured, in one call. When
it is non-empty the top-level sample fields are ignored.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. This is how a
backfill states WHICH window it measured; the server always owns the
observation clock, so there is no timestamp field.

branch.description:
Branch, CommitSha and Diffstat describe what the run produced; Error is the
failure when OK is false. Each is clamped, never rejected.

changed.description:
Changed says whether the run produced any commit. It is INDEPENDENT of OK: a
run can succeed and change nothing (there was nothing to do), and a run can
fail after committing some of its work. Two questions, two booleans.

commitSha.description:
CommitSha is the tip the run pushed, clamped to 128 characters. Empty when it
pushed nothing, which is the same case Changed reports false for.

diffstat.description:
Diffstat is the run's own summary of what it changed, as text, clamped to
64 KiB. Free-form: it is shown, never parsed.

error.description:
Error is why the run failed, clamped to 64 KiB. It is CLAMPED rather than
refused — a truncated reason is worth more than a rejected report, because a
rejected report leaves the durable workflow waiting forever.

id.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

ok.description: OK is whether the run succeeded; Changed whether it produced any commit.

runId.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

app.description: App is the service's CR name, from the path. It must be a DNS-1123 label.

env.description:
Env is REQUIRED and must be main, test or dev. A bare call does not default
to production, which is what closes the fat-finger and confused-deputy
hazard.

It carries no `validate:"required"`: the handler already refuses an empty env
with the sentence that names the three values, and a validator tag would
replace that sentence with a generic one. The requirement is stated here and
enforced there, once.

address.description:
Address is one of YOUR organisation's own published values (GET
/v1/risk/state reports them, and a search reports the one it fitted for you).
An address your organisation has not published is NOT FOUND — including one
another organisation published, because an address names a value and never
authorises reading it.

live.description:
Live turns the model out of shadow. It defaults to FALSE on every call, so
going live is always an explicit act and never a side effect of changing a
number.

Setting it requires an ADMIN of this organisation. Arming decides whether the
model may change an outcome at all — a payment frozen, a grant refused — for
every customer this organisation has, which is a governance act rather than a
tuning one. Stating the appetite and the sample needs no admin.

review.description:
Review is the share of the stream that may be sent for examination, in
(0, 0.5]. The alert threshold is derived from it as a quantile of the scores
actually observed, so the level is governed rather than tuned.

sample.description:
Sample is the share of below-the-line events retained for review, in
[0, 1]. It is the instrument that measures what the model missed; there are
no labels, so nothing else can.

cuts.description:
Cuts are the two RFC 3339 instants dividing train | val | test. Omit them to
take 70% and 85% of the window by time. Splitting is TEMPORAL and then
grouped by subject — a random split puts one device on both sides of the
line and the model memorises the entity instead of the behaviour.

dims.description:
Dims are the coordinates to carry, by published name. Empty takes the whole
surface. They are stored in the plane's own order, never the order given, so
two requests naming the same dims produce identical rows.

from.description:
From is where the event window opens, RFC 3339, INCLUSIVE. The window may
not be longer than the source's own retention: past that, its older half is
already gone and the dataset would silently be shorter than it says.

horizon.description:
Horizon is how many days a row must have aged before it may be admitted. It
is what keeps a fact that was not yet knowable at scoring time out of a
training set: a chargeback lands 30 to 120 days after the transaction it
condemns, so 120 for the payment lane and 14 for signup abuse. Zero admits
the whole window and is honest only where the outcome is immediate.

kind.description:
Kind narrows to one subject kind — person, session or account. Empty takes
every kind.

name.description:
Name identifies the dataset across its versions: lower-case letters, digits
and hyphens, starting with a letter.

rows.description: Rows caps the materialisation. Zero takes the plane's own bound.

seed.description:
Seed decides WHICH subjects are admitted when the window holds more rows
than the cap allows. It is recorded on the version, so a capped dataset is
reproducible rather than being whichever rows the store returned first.
Omit it to seed from the dataset's name.

to.description:
To is where the window ends, EXCLUSIVE, so two datasets meeting at one
instant share no row. A materialisation reads less than this — the end is
pulled back by Horizon, and the lineage reports the window it actually read.

before.description:
Before disposes of assertions WRITTEN before this instant, RFC 3339. It is
measured against the server clock at the write and not against the event
or observation times, both of which the asserting caller supplies — a
tenant that could back-date could delete a compliance record on demand.

at.description:
At is when it happened, RFC 3339. Empty means now. It must sit inside the
thirty-day window the aggregates keep and no more than two minutes ahead of
this plane's clock; anything outside that is REFUSED rather than quietly
accepted, because a future timestamp moves the aggregates' leading edge and
leaves every later event for that subject reading as though it never
happened. History older than the window is folded in from your own event
surface, not through this endpoint.

device.description:
Device is the device fingerprint, if any. It is the axis that surfaces
several nominally unrelated subjects acting as one.

id.description:
ID is the caller's own stable identifier for the event. It selects the
below-the-line review sample by hash, so a counter would make the sample
steerable — use the id the event already has.

kind.description:
Kind is whose behaviour this is: person, session or account. It namespaces
the subject, so a person and an account that share an identifier stay two
subjects.

nano.description:
Nano is the value moved, in nano-USD. Omit it for an event that moves no
money: the value features then read BLIND rather than being told the amount
was zero, and the difference is reported on the model state.

peer.description:
Peer is the counterparty, if any. It is an aggregation axis of its own —
"unfamiliar" is a fact about a relationship and not about either party.

subject.description: Subject is the identifier on that kind.

hold.description:
Hold is the state to put them in: true places the hold, false releases it.
One op both ways, because a hold that can be placed and not released pins a
compliance record past every retention boundary with nothing able to let it
go — and an operator who cannot release a hold stops placing them.

ids.description:
IDs are the content digests of the records, as returned by the write and
by the read. They name records in THIS tenant's plane; an id belonging to
anybody else names nothing here, because the statement runs against this
tenant's own file and there is no other file it could reach.

at.description:
At is the event's own instant, RFC 3339. It is part of the event's IDENTITY
and not a filter: it is matched exactly, to the second, against the `at` the
assertions were filed under, so an instant a second off names a different
event and resolves to nothing. It is also what this event's as-of is measured
from — At plus the horizon.

kind.description:
Kind is the judged entity's type, from the closed set: account, agent,
merchant, payout, person, session or transaction. One outside it is refused
rather than answered `unlabelled`, because it could only ever match nothing
and the caller would read a real absence into a typo.

subject.description:
Subject is the entity id in the tenant's own namespace, at most 512 bytes. It
is matched EXACTLY against what was recorded — this is a lookup, not a search,
and no prefix, pattern or normalisation is applied.

at.description: At is when the judged event happened, RFC 3339.

confidence.description:
Confidence in [0,1]. A processor chargeback is 1; an analyst's hunch is
not. It breaks a tie WITHIN a precedence rank and can never lift a weak
source above a strong one — otherwise every caller would send 1.

A litigation hold is NOT a field here. It is a fact about the record and
not about the world, so it is not part of what was asserted, it is not in
the content digest, and it has its own op — which is also the only way one
can be released. Carried here it was silently a no-op on any record that
already existed: the digest was the same, the insert was ignored, and the
caller was told `duplicate` while the hold it asked for was never placed.

disposition.description:
Disposition is productive, unproductive, or empty for an explicit
unjudged — the AML engine's own vocabulary, verbatim.

evidence.description:
Evidence points at the record this conclusion came from: a dispute id, a
case id, a decision id. Required, because a label with no evidence cannot
be defended when the adverse action it fed is challenged.

kind.description:
Kind is what the subject is: account, agent, merchant, payout, person,
session or transaction. Closed, because a typo in an open field would shard
a tenant's labels into a partition nothing reads and nothing would say so.

seen.description:
Seen is when this assertion became KNOWABLE, RFC 3339. It is required and
it is not At: a chargeback lands 30 to 120 days after the transaction it
judges, and a training set joined on At alone knows the future. Everything
this plane does to prevent leakage is computed from Seen.

source.description:
Source is who asserted: chargeoff, dispute, case, refund, review or
sample. It is the primary term of the precedence rule, so it is closed —
an unknown source has no rank and a conflict with it could not be resolved.

subject.description: Subject identifies the thing being judged, in the tenant's own namespace.

labels.description:
Labels is the batch. Each member is judged on its own: one refusal does
not discard the rest, because a webhook redelivering five disputes must
not lose four of them to one malformed fifth.

events.description:
Events are the things that happened, oldest first. An empty batch is
refused: learning nothing is not an operation.

horizon.description:
Horizon is how many days an event must age before it may be resolved at
all, and it is the whole of the no-leakage rule. 120 for the payment lane
(past the Visa and Mastercard dispute windows), 14 for signup abuse.
Unstated takes 120.

now.description:
Now moves the observation instant BACKWARDS, RFC 3339. It exists so a
BACKTEST can resolve labels as the plane stood at a past moment; without it,
every backtest would score a model against knowledge that arrived after the
decision it is being scored on. An instant after the server clock is
refused: a backtest resolves the past, and a future one would declare
unmatured events matured and hand a training set negatives for rows whose
chargeback has not had time to arrive.

subjects.description:
Subjects are the exact events being judged. Each carries its own event
time, because the as-of that keeps the future out is derived from that
instant plus the horizon — one as-of over a whole batch would give a
January row six extra months of hindsight.

One entry per DISTINCT (kind, subject, at): naming an event twice answers
once, because an event resolved twice would list its own winner as a
contrary claim and would hand a materialiser duplicate training rows.

event.description:
Event is the thing to judge. It is judged against the caller's OWN model
and nothing is learned from it.

days.description:
Days is how much of the organisation's own history to replay, 1 to 400.
Zero takes thirty.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

deploymentId.description:
DeploymentID is the deployment to redeploy. Omit it to return to the
previous release.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

pattern.description: Pattern is the URL pattern to bind, e.g. "acme.com/api/*".

script.description:
Script is the Worker script to dispatch to. Omit it to leave the pattern
bound to no script, which is how Cloudflare expresses "bypass the Worker here".

zone.description: Zone is the 32-hex Cloudflare zone id, from the path.

chain.description: Chain is the registry id, from the URL.

id.description: ID is echoed back untouched.

method.description: Method is the RPC method, e.g. eth_getBalance.

params.description: Params is the method's parameters, passed through unread.

action.description: Action is the name of the connector action to invoke.

auth.description:
Auth is the caller's resolved credential for the connector, handed to the
action verbatim. Its shape is whatever the connector's auth descriptor
declares (a token string, an object), so it is opaque here.

id.description: ID is the connector to run, from the path.

props.description: Props are the action's input properties, keyed by property name.

env.description:
Env is the run's environment. Keys must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`;
a variable marked `secret: true` is sealed into KMS.

gpu.description: GPU is how many GPUs the run asks for; a negative value is 400.

image.description: Image is the container image to run. Required.

maxScale.description:
MaxScale above the floor declares an autoscaling ceiling; 0 means no
autoscaler at all — a fixed run at the floor.

minScale.description: MinScale is the replica floor, clamped to the deployment's limit.

name.description:
Name is the run's name, and the slug is derived from it. Required, and it
must resolve to `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$`. Re-running the same
name updates that run in place.

port.description: Port is the container port the run listens on.

runtime.description:
Runtime is accepted for the client contract and echoed nowhere: the image
IS the runtime unit.

shape.description:
Shape is a compute size label, echoed back; sizing is the operator's
default. Defaults to "auto".

dataset.description:
Dataset is the set to score, which must belong to the caller's org and hold
at least one ACTIVE example.

judge.description:
Judge is the judge to grade with. Omitted, the model under test grades
itself against a default correctness criterion under the score name
"llm-judge".

limit.description:
Limit caps how many examples this run scores. It defaults to 20, and
anything above 100 falls back to that default.

model.description: Model is the model under test.

runName.description:
RunName labels the run and is generated from the clock when omitted. It
must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$.

arch.description: Arch is the target architecture for the artifact lane.

args.description:
Args are --build-arg values. They are what lets several images off ONE
Dockerfile mean different things — the sandbox classes are three entries
differing only by STAGE. Validated at the k8s choke point, with VERSION and
REVISION taking precedence: those are receipts the builder derives from the
tag and the commit, and a caller that could overwrite them could make an
image lie about which commit it is.

binaries.description:
Binaries selects the ARTIFACT lane (artifact.go): build what the repo's
hanzo.yml `binaries:` block declares — a Go binary, an npm tarball, a Rust
binary — and publish it to hanzoai/s3 instead of pushing an image. It is the
same recipe hanzoai/ci reads, sent verbatim, so `image` is meaningless here
and must be absent.

branch.description: Branch is the branch to build when no SHA or Ref is given.

bucket.description: Bucket mirrors hanzo.yml's `bucket:` — where the artifact lane publishes.

context.description: Context is the build context path within the repo.

dockerTarget.description: DockerTarget is the multi-stage build target to stop at.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile is the path to build from; empty uses the zero-config frontend.

image.description:
Image is the output image ref to push. Required on the image lane, and it
must target a registry namespace the caller's org owns.

os.description: OS is the target operating system for the artifact lane.

ref.description: Ref is the git ref to build when no SHA is given.

repo.description: Repo is the repository clone URL to build. Required on the image lane.

sha.description: SHA is the commit to pin; it wins over Ref and Branch.

tag.description:
Tag is the publish path segment, so both entry points write ONE index at ONE
URL. It defaults to the pinned ref, and must be named explicitly for a
branch.

documentIds.description: DocumentIDs are data room document ids to raise a signature request over. Required.

signers.description: Signers are the recipients, each a name and an email. Required.

chainId.description:
ChainID is the EVM chain the Safe transaction is bound to. 0 uses the
wallet's own chain, or the Hanzo L1 (36963) when it is chain-agnostic.

data.description: Data is the call data, hex-encoded.

nonce.description: Nonce is the Safe's transaction nonce.

to.description: To is the transaction's target address.

value.description: Value is the native-token amount to send, as a decimal string in wei.

gpuModel.description:
GPUModel names the representative accelerator ("GB10"); GPUs carries how
many. A heterogeneous host names its first card rather than inventing a
summary.

gpuUtil.description:
GPUUtil is accelerator utilization as a fraction 0..1; the warehouse clamps
anything outside that.

gpus.description: GPUs is how many accelerators this reading covers.

host.description: Host is the node's hostname, for display.

memFree.description: MemFree is host memory still available, in BYTES.

memUsed.description: MemUsed is host memory in use, in BYTES.

unit.description:
Unit is the reporting node's own id — the same id it registered under, and
the key the board joins this series onto. Required.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description:
ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339. Empty is
allowed; anything else that is not RFC3339 is refused.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. Empty is allowed;
anything else that is not RFC3339 is refused.

content.description:
Content is the source to scan. It is NEVER stored: what persists is the
finding, with a masked preview and a fingerprint.

path.description:
Path is where the file lives, recorded on any finding so a result can be
located in the tree it came from.

categories.description:
Categories is the closed set of labels a CATEGORICAL score may carry. A
CATEGORICAL rubric with none is refused.

dataType.description: DataType is NUMERIC (the default), CATEGORICAL or BOOLEAN.

maxValue.description: MaxValue is the inclusive ceiling a NUMERIC score must stay under, finite.

minValue.description:
MinValue is the inclusive floor a NUMERIC score must clear. It must be
finite and must not exceed MaxValue.

name.description:
Name is the score name this rubric governs, matching
^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. The name is the key, so re-posting one
replaces its rules.

comment.description: Comment is the grader's reasoning, truncated at 2000 characters.

dataType.description:
DataType is NUMERIC, CATEGORICAL or BOOLEAN. A declared rubric overrides it
— a caller cannot claim a type the org's rubric contradicts.

datasetItemId.description: ItemID attaches the score to one graded example.

datasetName.description: Dataset attaches the score to one dataset.

name.description:
Name is the score name. A rubric of the same name, if the org has declared
one, decides this score's type and the values it may take.

runName.description: RunName attaches the score to one run.

stringValue.description:
StringValue is the label of a CATEGORICAL score, which must be one the
rubric allows.

traceId.description: TraceID attaches the score to one model call.

value.description:
Value is the numeric score, which must be finite: NaN and Inf are refused.
A BOOLEAN score takes 0 or 1.

doctypes.description:
DocTypes restricts retrieval to a subset of the indexed knowledge doctypes
(kb.page, kb.memory, kb.source). An empty or foreign list reads all of them.

limit.description: Limit bounds the hits returned. Default 10, maximum 50.

project.description: Project narrows retrieval to one project scope.

query.description: Query is the natural-language question. Required.

data.description:
Data is the record. What may be in it depends on the section, and every
section's required fields are validated: a control is held to the same rule
a committed one is, a subprocessor must say what it is for, an update must
carry the date it describes.

id.description:
ID is the record's id. Omit it on a create and one is minted; the
single-valued sections (profile, risk) hold one record whatever is named.

kind.description: Kind is the section being written. The URL is the authority.

ord.description:
Ord orders this record within its section, ascending, ties broken by id.
It is the organization's own ordering — the page renders in it.

url.description: URL is the page, absolute and http or https.

target.description:
Target is a domain, a subdomain or a single page URL. A domain summarises the
whole site; a URL summarises that page.

keywords.description: Keywords are the phrases. At least one; blanks are dropped.

language.description: Language is the ISO code. Defaults to "en".

limit.description: Limit is how many domains to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to 100.

location.description: Location is the market, as the upstream's numeric code. Defaults to 2840.

keywords.description: Keywords are the seeds. At least one; blanks are dropped.

language.description: Language is the ISO code. Defaults to "en".

limit.description:
Limit is how many phrases to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to 100. It is what
this call is priced on, because the upstream charges per row.

location.description: Location is the market, as the upstream's numeric code. Defaults to 2840.

keywords.description: Keywords are the phrases. At least one; blanks are dropped.

language.description: Language is the ISO code. Defaults to "en".

location.description:
Location is the market, as the upstream's numeric code. Defaults to 2840,
the United States.

domain.description: Domain is the site, with or without a subdomain — "hanzo.ai", "docs.hanzo.ai".

language.description: Language is the ISO code. Defaults to "en".

limit.description: Limit is how many placements to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to 100.

location.description: Location is the market, as the upstream's numeric code. Defaults to 2840.

host.description:
Host is where the HOSTING identity forwards a connection — an address the
host device itself can reach, "127.0.0.1" for a server on the device.

name.description:
Name is the service's name within the org — a DNS label. The fabric knows
the service as "<name>.<org>" and answers for it at "<name>.<org>.zt".

port.description: Port is the port beside Host, and the one the DNS name intercepts.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

env.description:
Env is the app's whole environment set, REPLACING what it had. Keys must
match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`; a variable marked `secret: true` is
sealed into KMS and blanked in the database.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

config.description:
Config is the product's non-secret configuration, stored verbatim. Bounded at
64 KiB once serialized. Omit it to store an empty object.

product.description:
Product is the catalog slug, from the PATH. zip binds the path last, so the
URL names the product being written whatever a body field claims.

secrets.description:
Secrets are the secret fields, by name. Each VALUE is sealed into KMS and
never reaches this deployment's database; a value that is empty or equal to
the mask the read path returns means "unchanged" and is skipped, so a console
round-trip cannot blank a stored secret. A key must match
^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$, a value is bounded at 8 KiB, and an org may hold
at most 64 secret fields per product.

digest.description:
Digest is a pre-computed 32-byte digest as hex, with or without the 0x
prefix. When present it is signed verbatim and message is ignored.

message.description:
Message is arbitrary text to hash with Keccak256 and sign. Used only when
digest is empty.

id.description: ID is the document to send for signature, from the path.

signers.description:
Signers are the people who must sign, by name and email. At least one is
required.

content.description: Content is the SKILL.md body. Required, at most 256 KiB.

description.description: Description is the one-line summary discovery shows for the skill.

name.description:
Name is the skill's id within the org: one lowercase path segment
(a-z0-9, _ or -). Writing an existing name REVISES that skill.

handle.description:
Handle is the account's public name on the network, as the customer knows it
(`@acme`). Trimmed and bounded at 1024 characters.

Example: "@acme"

provider.description:
Provider is the network this account is on: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x. Anything else is refused rather
than coerced, because a stored account on a network that does not exist can
never be published through.

Example: "x"

status.description:
Status is the connection lifecycle: connected, disconnected or error.
Omitted means connected. Only a connected account is a publish target.

handle.description:
Handle is the account's public name on the network. Omitting it BLANKS the
stored handle: this is a replacement, not a merge.

Example: "@acme"

provider.description:
Provider is the network this account is on: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x.

Example: "x"

status.description:
Status is the connection lifecycle: connected, disconnected or error.
Omitting it RESETS the account to connected.

channel.description:
Channel is the network to publish to: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x.

Example: "x"

content.description:
Content is the post's text. Required — an empty body is a 400 — and bounded
at 8192 characters, comfortably above every network's own limit.

Example: "Shipping today."

media.description:
Media is the post's attached media as URLs, at most 10, each bounded at 1024
characters. Blank entries are dropped. Omitting it CLEARS any stored media.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when to publish, as a unix timestamp in SECONDS. 0 means
unscheduled. A negative value is clamped to 0. It only matters for a post
whose status is scheduled.

status.description:
Status is the post's lifecycle state: draft, scheduled, published or failed.
Omitted means draft. The transient publishing claim is never settable here —
accepting it from a request would let a caller wedge or replay the guard that
stops two publishers double-posting the same row.

channel.description:
Channel is the network to publish to: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x.

Example: "x"

content.description:
Content is the post's text. Required on every update, and bounded at 8192
characters.

Example: "Shipping today."

media.description:
Media is the post's attached media as URLs, at most 10. Omitting it CLEARS
any stored media: this is a replacement, not a merge.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when to publish, as a unix timestamp in SECONDS. 0 means
unscheduled. Moving it into the past here does NOT publish the post — that is
the scheduler's to notice, or the publish operation's.

status.description:
Status is the post's lifecycle state: draft, scheduled, published or failed.
Omitting it RESETS the post to draft.

name.description:
Name is the space's name, matching ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$ — the
shape a drive name takes too, so a caller learns one rule. It is validated AS
GIVEN and never lower-cased for you: a client that creates "Photos" and then
lists "photos" would be reading a space it did not make, so mixed case is a
clean 400.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

enabled.description:
Enabled publishes the script on <script>.<subdomain>.workers.dev when true,
and withdraws it when false.

script.description: Script is the Worker script name, from the path.

email.description: Email is the subject's contact email, sealed at rest.

kind.description: Kind is the party type: "individual" (KYC) or "business" (KYB).

name.description: Name is the subject's name, sealed at rest.

ref.description: Ref is the org's own opaque external id for this subject.

files.description: Files is the batch to scan, at most 500 files and 8 MiB of content in total.

project.description:
Project names the sub-scope the scan is filed under. It must be a slug; omit
it and the caller's project header is used instead.

channel.description:
Channel is the Slack channel the notifier posts to — an id (C…/G…), a
#name, or a bare name. Required.

events.description:
Events narrows delivery to these lifecycle kinds (push.landed,
deploy.live, deploy.failed). Omit it to receive every deliverable kind; a
kind that is never posted to Slack is refused rather than silently dropped.

name.description: Name is the repo to subscribe, from the :name path segment.

attempts.description:
Attempts is how many times to try each item; the harness's default applies
when it is omitted.

benchmarks.description:
Benchmarks are the catalog ids to run. At least one is required, and every id
must be in the catalog.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is your own chat-completions URL, for benchmarking a model this arena
does not host. Either this or model is required.

model.description: Model is the catalog model id to run. Either this or endpoint is required.

actor.description:
Actor is the identity the sync writes as, used as the loop guard so its own
writes do not re-trigger it. Defaults to the deployment's GIT_SYNC_ACTOR.

direction.description: Direction is both (the default), pull, push or off.

kind.description: Kind is what is being synced. Only "git" today, which is also the default.

run.description: Run reconciles once immediately after the upsert, in the background.

source.description: Source is the upstream end. Required.

target.description:
Target is the downstream end. Optional for git: a native repository named
after the source is derived when it is omitted.

trigger.description: Trigger is what starts a reconcile: webhook (the default), poll or manual.

capacity.description:
Capacity is a human summary of the machine's size, up to 256 characters. Prose
only; a scheduler reads Spec.

host.description:
Host is the hostname sessions on this machine will report. It is what makes a
re-link IDEMPOTENT: the same (org, host, owner) refreshes the existing row and
answers 200, while a request with no host always creates a new target and
answers 201. It never adopts a row owned by somebody else.

kind.description:
Kind is laptop | cloud | gpu | cluster | machine. Empty registers a `machine`;
anything outside the five is a 400.

label.description:
Label is the name to show for this machine, up to 128 characters. REQUIRED —
it is the only field here a person reads.

metrics.description:
Metrics is a live sample, and sending one IS A HEARTBEAT: it refreshes the row
and starts the 90-second liveness window, and it is appended to the fleet
series as one point. Its own `at` is ignored — the server stamps the time, so
a client can never age or backdate its own machine. Omit it to register a
machine without claiming it is alive.

spec.description:
Spec is the machine's static capability — os, arch, cores, RAM, accelerators.
Every field is bounded on write and at most 32 accelerators are accepted, so
what comes back may be clamped. Omit it for a destination nothing probes.

status.description:
Status is online | offline | draining. Empty registers `online`. It states
INTENT — a heartbeat is what decides whether an online machine is actually
reachable, so declaring online does not make it so.

agentOfRecord.description: AgentOfRecord puts us on file as the entity's agent, yearly.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation.

structure.description: Structure is the entity being formed: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

brands.description:
Brands are the brands whose console shows it. Omit for every brand its
category admits.

category.description: Category is the id of an EXISTING category to file it under. Required.

description.description: Description is the one line shown beneath the name.

href.description:
Href is the absolute URL an external product launches. Give this or route,
never both.

icon.description: Icon names the icon the surface renders, e.g. "Database".

id.description: ID is the taxon slug to write, from the path.

name.description: Name is the display name. Required.

order.description: Order is where it sits within its category, ascending.

published.description:
Published is whether it is shown. Omitted means published — a taxon someone
took the trouble to write is meant to be seen, and hiding one is the
deliberate act.

route.description:
Route is the in-console path it opens, e.g. "/vector". Give this or href,
never both.

tags.description: Tags are free-form labels for search and grouping across categories.

id.description: ID is the room to say it in, from the path.

space.description:
Space names the space holding the room. Body-only: a query string may not
redirect a write.

text.description:
Text is what to say, as plain text. It is wrapped in the client's markup on
the way in, so a caller writes words rather than HTML.

bindings.description:
Bindings REPLACES what the room is about, wholly. It is a replace and
not a merge because a caller that cannot remove a binding would have no way
to correct a wrong one, and an empty list sent explicitly is how a room
is unbound. Absent (null) leaves the existing list alone.

id.description:
ID is the room to bind, from the path. The URL is the authority; a body
carrying another id cannot redirect the write.

life.description:
Life sets the lifecycle intent: "standing" or "bound". Any other
value is refused rather than stored, so a reader never has to interpret a
third one. Empty leaves the current intent unchanged.

space.description:
Space names the space holding the room. It is required, because
a room id is unique only within one and searching every space for a
matching id would make the write's target depend on iteration order.

bindings.description: Bindings are what the room is about, each "<kind>:<ref>".

life.description: Life is the lifecycle intent, "standing" or "bound"; empty reads standing.

members.description:
Members are the account uuids in the room. A public room may open empty —
anyone in the org can find it — and a private one that names nobody is
refused rather than created unreachable.

name.description:
Name is what a person sees in a sidebar — "bugfix-1010", not "#bugfix-1010".
The sigil is how a client DRAWS a room, and storing it would put it in the
name twice the first time a client added its own.

private.description:
Private restricts the room to its members. Public is the default because a
room nobody can find is the more surprising of the two.

space.description:
Space is where the room is opened. Optional: an org with one space has no
choice to make, so it does not have to state one. An org with several must,
because picking for it would make the room's home depend on iteration order.

topic.description: Topic is the room's one-line subject.

body.description:
Body is the text/template source. Required. Every {{.key}} it references must
be declared in Fields, or the save is refused rather than rendering a blank
into a contract later.

category.description:
Category groups the template: formation, equity, ops or sales. Optional when
overriding a built-in, which supplies its own.

counselReview.description:
CounselReview marks a template whose documents must carry the counsel notice.
It can be raised but never lowered: a formation or equity template is always
counsel-review, and an override of a counsel-review built-in stays one.

fields.description:
Fields declares the merge fields the body consumes. Every declared field is
REQUIRED at generation — the engine fails closed on a missing one.

id.description:
ID is the template to override, from the path. Overriding a built-in id
inherits that built-in's category, title and counsel-review posture.

title.description: Title is the template's display name. Required unless a built-in supplies it.

arguments.description:
Arguments is the tool's own input object, passed through verbatim to
whichever source owns it.

name.description: Name is the tool to run, exactly as GET /v1/tools reports it.

amountCents.description: AmountCents is how much to charge, in cents of Currency. Required.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO-4217 code to charge in. Empty takes the deployment's
own default.

paymentMethodId.description: MethodID names a card the subject already saved, for the saved-card endpoint.

sourceId.description:
SourceID is a single-use card token from the payment form, for the token
endpoint. It is vaulted as part of the charge, so a caller never holds card
numbers and this service never sees one.

authCode.description:
AuthCode is the transfer authorization the losing registrar issued. It is
required.

domain.description: Domain is the name to move in. It is required.

years.description: Years is the term to buy on transfer, defaulting to 1.

doctype.description: DocType is the content type to act on, from the path.

name.description: Name is the document to act on, from the path.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is an ISO-8601 go-live time handed to the channel's own scheduler;
"" distributes now.

to.description:
To is the lifecycle state to move to. Required, and the move must be a legal
edge from the item's current state.

accept.description:
Accept must be true when the centre states an NDA. The text accepted is
recorded verbatim on the request, so a later edit to the NDA cannot rewrite
what this party agreed to.

email.description:
Email is where the grant will be sent, and the ONLY address the resulting
link admits. Required.

item.description:
Item names one published item to ask for. Optional; omitting it asks for
everything released on request.

party.description: Party is the company the asker is from. Optional, and recorded as stated.

reason.description:
Reason is why they want it. Optional, and recorded as stated — it is what the
person deciding reads.

slug.description: Slug is the centre's public address, taken from the path.

days.description:
Days is how long the grant stays open, from now. Optional; 14 by default and
365 at most — a longer release is describing a customer relationship rather
than a document.

id.description: ID is the request to answer, taken from the path.

note.description:
Note is why. Recorded on the request either way, and it is what the record
shows a year later.

document.description:
Document replaces the file the item points at — this is how a report is
superseded by its next edition. The new document must already exist in the
caller org's own store.

framework.description: Framework replaces the standard it speaks to.

id.description: ID is the item to change, taken from the path.

name.description: Name replaces its title.

retired.description:
Retired withdraws the item, or true→false restores it. A retired item leaves
the public centre at once and can no longer be granted; grants already made
over it stand, because they are part of the record.

summary.description: Summary replaces the line about it.

tier.description:
Tier moves it between public and gated. Moving an auditor-signed item to
public is refused.

attester.description:
Attester is who vouched for it: "self" for anything the org states itself, or
"auditor" for anything an independent auditor put their name to. REQUIRED, and
anything other than "self" is read as "auditor" — the safe direction, since an
auditor-signed item can only ever be released on request.

body.description:
Body is the item's content for the kinds that are text rather than a file: an
article, a subprocessor entry, a dated note.

document.description:
Document is a data-room document holding the item's bytes, uploaded first
through POST /v1/dataroom/documents. Optional: an item can be content with no
file. The document must already exist in the caller org's own store.

framework.description:
Framework is the standard it speaks to. Optional and free text — the value is
the org's own, not a list this API keeps.

kind.description:
Kind is what the item is: report, letter, policy, questionnaire, subprocessor,
article or update. Required.

name.description: Name is the item's title. Required.

summary.description: Summary is a line about it. Optional.

tier.description:
Tier is who may read it: "public" or "gated". It DEFAULTS TO GATED and
anything that is not exactly "public" is gated, so an item published by a
caller that says nothing is private and someone has to release it on purpose.
"public" is refused for an auditor-signed item.

name.description: Name is the centre's display name. Required to publish.

publish.description:
Publish makes the centre answer at its public address. False withdraws it: the
address stops answering while every item, grant and record stays exactly as it
was, so withdrawing is reversible and loses nothing.

slug.description:
Slug is the public address to answer at — a lowercase label of letters,
digits and hyphens. Required to publish, unique across the deployment, and one
org holds one: publishing under a new address MOVES the centre rather than
leaving the old one answering.

avatar.description:
Avatar and Emoji re-draw the agent. Sending either replaces the pair, so
setting an image clears a glyph and "" for both goes back to the initial —
there is no state where a row holds two answers.

computeRef.description: ComputeRef re-binds (or, with "", unbinds) the visor machine. Opaque here.

description.description: Description replaces the line other agents read in the tool catalogue.

emoji.description:
Emoji re-draws the agent as a glyph. Sending either of the pair replaces
BOTH, so setting a glyph clears an image and "" for both goes back to the
initial — there is no state where a row holds two answers.

executionMode.description:
ExecutionMode switches between one-shot and long-running. The RESULTING
mode+schedule are validated together, so switching to long-running without a
stored or supplied cron is refused rather than accepted into an agent the
scheduler would skip forever. A switch INTO long-running counts against the
per-org cap and can be a 409.

instructions.description:
Instructions replaces the system prompt whole, up to 32 KiB. There is no
append: a prompt is one text, and sending "" clears it.

model.description:
Model re-points the agent at another model, checked against the gateway's
served catalogue exactly as create checks it. Empty STRING is refused — say
nothing to keep the current one. Past runs keep the model that served them.

ref.description: Ref is the agent to update — its public id or org-unique name, from the path.

schedule.description:
Schedule replaces the cron. It is validated against the mode this update
leaves behind, and dropped if that mode is one-shot.

serviceAccountId.description:
ServiceAccountID re-points (or, with "", clears) the IAM service account a
scheduled run is billed as. Clearing it puts that spend back on the org.

tools.description:
Tools replaces the whole allow-list, it does not add to it. Sending [] takes
every tool away, which is the only way to say that.

account.description: Account is the provider ad-account this campaign runs on (Meta act_<id>). Optional.

budget.description: Budget is the campaign budget in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

name.description: Name is the campaign's display label. Required; trimmed and bounded to 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the campaign goal as the provider names it. Optional, bounded to 1024 bytes.

platform.description: Platform is the ad network: meta, google, tiktok or x. Empty defaults to meta.

spend.description: Spend is the amount spent so far in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

status.description: Status is the lifecycle state: draft, active, paused or completed. Empty defaults to draft.

description.description: Description is a free-text label for the console. Optional, clipped to 1024 bytes.

events.description:
Events are NATS subject patterns to subscribe to. An empty or omitted list
means EVERY event. Max 64 patterns, each max 256 bytes.

status.description: Status is "active" or "disabled". Empty defaults to active.

url.description:
URL is the https:// address each matching event is POSTed to. Required,
max 2048 bytes; http:// and every other scheme is refused.

agentOfRecord.description: AgentOfRecord includes our agent fee, which most entities owe someone.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state the entity stands in.

structure.description: Structure is the entity kind: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket to upload into, from the path.

key.description:
Key is the object key relative to the bucket root. It is path-cleaned, so a
"../" cannot escape the bucket, and an empty or unclean key is 400.

handle.description:
Handle is the display name shown on a listed row: 1-40 characters of letters,
digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a listing
opt-in it defaults to the caller's username.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the caller's row to other viewers of the board when true, and
anonymizes it when false.

nonce.description: Nonce is the value GET /v1/validator/challenge issued for this slot.

signature.description:
Signature is the wallet's personal_sign over the challenge message, hex with
a 0x prefix.

tokenId.description:
TokenID is the Validator-tier GenesisNFT token id being claimed. It IS the
validator slot.

id.description: ID is the verification to decide, from the path.

status.description:
Status is the reviewer's decision: "reviewer_confirmed" (a pass) or
"manual_review" (withheld for review) — never a provider status.

email.description: Email is an inline subject's contact email, sealed at rest.

kind.description: Kind is an inline subject's party type: "individual" (KYC) or "business" (KYB).

name.description: Name is an inline subject's name, sealed at rest.

ref.description: Ref is the org's own opaque external id for an inline subject.

subjectId.description: SubjectID names an existing subject to verify; empty creates one inline.

repoUrl.description:
RepoURL is what to claim: a repository (github.com/owner/name) or a whole
OWNER (github.com/owner, no repository segment). gitlab.com is accepted too.

language.description:
Language narrows the search to a locale, BCP-47-ish ("en", "ja"). Empty
means no narrowing.

max_sources.description: MaxSources caps how many pages are read. Empty means the mode's own budget.

mode.description:
Mode is how much work to do: `search` (fast, one pass), `news` (recency
biased), `research` (a plan and several rounds) or `deep` (the widest
survey). Empty means research.

q.description: Q is the question, in plain language. Required.

sources.description:
Sources narrows where the evidence comes from: any of `web`, `news`,
`academic`, `github`, `reddit`, `x`. Each becomes a site-scoped search, so
`["x"]` researches X/Twitter posts rather than the open web.

language.description:
Language narrows the engines to a locale, BCP-47-ish ("en", "ja", "de").
Empty means no narrowing.

q.description:
Q is the query. Required — an empty one is refused rather than answered
with the whole web.

info.description: Generated by `cargo run --features genspec --bin genspec`. The SOURCE is the Hanzo Cloud API document hanzo-inc/cloud@39bc7972da6174b94fc17fb20465758613616d6d sha256:2dd32162f86963c080b1139549d593139ba6a3cb30533ef5abaf04881e7ef183, and it is the ONLY source: it enumerates the operations, and carries their prose and their reflected shapes. Nothing is joined in — an operation absent here is an operation no cloud router registers, which is what makes a phantom command impossible rather than rare. Never hand-edited: `genproduct` derives src/commands/product/generated.rs from this and nothing else. RELAY DOORS, 0: a /v1/<product>/{wildcardN} route is the document declaring a subtree reachable without naming what is behind it, and those addresses are the only places a generated CLI knowingly falls short of what cloud serves. There are none.

Answers the richer self-view: the same lifetime accrued, pending and paid commission and payout history, plus the caller's downline broken out by upline LEVEL — direct, second, third — each with the rate paid at that level and how many orgs sit there.
Answers the caller's own commission ledger: per period, the margin it earned against and the commission taken from that margin; and per referred org, that referral's aggregate contribution.
